title: " Network \/ TLS Dataset Phishing detection"
authors: Ashvini jadhav; Pankaj R. Chandre
abstract: "This dataset is collected to support infrastructure-level phishing and malicious hosting detection from encrypted network traffic without decryption. It provides a large-scale collection of network and TLS infrastructure features derived from TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 traffic, enabling the detection of phishing URLs directly at the transport layer. The dataset contains 126,063 network sessions and URLs, each represented by 197 numeric attributes describing TLS handshake behavior, protocol versions, server implementation fingerprints, timing statistics, and HTTP\/HTTPS error patterns. Unlike traditional phishing datasets that primarily rely on URL strings or webpage content, this dataset captures low-level transport and application-layer characteristics that reveal anomalous and deceptive infrastructure behavior. The dataset is labeled for binary classification (benign 0 vs. phishing 1). It is suitable for training and evaluating machine learning and deep learning models for network-based phishing detection, malicious hosting identification, and infrastructure anomaly detection. It is derived from TLS traffic traces and supports research on phishing detection in encrypted traffic without payload inspection. Baseline experiments reported in prior studies using Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM achieve accuracies of 97.63%, 97.07%, and 97.40%, respectively, demonstrating the effectiveness of infrastructure-level signals. In addition, experiments with feature optimization and deep learning models (MLP, CNN, LSTM, GRU) show that dimensionality can be reduced by 25\u201350% while further improving detection performance to nearly 98% accuracy with lower computational overhead. Owing to its high dimensionality, heterogeneity, and scale, this dataset is particularly valuable for research on feature selection, representation learning, class imbalance handling, encrypted traffic analysis, and scalable cybersecurity analytics."

title: "ANF-IoT: A Unified Multi-Protocol IoT Dataset for Faulty Traffic and DDoS Attacks Detection"
authors: Md Toufiqur Rahman (9655855); Makhduma F. Saiyed; Irfan Al‐Anbagi
abstract: "Internet of Things (IoT) networks are widely used in critical infrastructure environments such as healthcare and industrial systems, where Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) rely on benchmark datasets for training and evaluation. However, most existing datasets consider only normal and attack traffic, ignoring faulty traffic caused by communication errors, device malfunctions, or software anomalies. This creates a gap in current datasets, as faulty traffic is not included as a separate class despite its impact on detection performance. In many cases, faulty traffic resembles Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks, leading to misclassification. To address this gap, we present ANF-IoT (Attack, Normal, and Fault IoT), a multiprotocol dataset generated on a real testbed. The testbed consists of more than 50 physical devices, including Raspberry Pi 5,Raspberry Pi 4, Raspberry Pi 3, and PicoW. The dataset captures traffic across five protocols (UDP, TCP, MQTT, HTTP, TLS) with three explicitly labelled classes: normal, attack, and faulty, resulting in 3.25 million records. The dataset reflects realistic IoT conditions, where the attack class covers DDoS scenarios, while the faulty class captures fault-driven traffic that mimics DDoS. This behaviour is validated using the Mann\u2013Whitney U test and Cliff\u2019s delta, with a moderate similarity design between attack and faulty traffic, while normal traffic remains clearly distinguishable. A five-stage data validation pipeline is used to ensure a clean, leakage-free, and machine learning (ML)-ready dataset. Experimental evaluation using nine classical machine learning models and tabular deep learning models shows an accuracy of approximately 83.5% and 78% F1-score for the faulty class. The result with these per-flow models reflects a non-trivial characteristic of such an ANF-IoT dataset. Although these models separate normal traffic from adversarial classes with above 93% accuracy, they cannot fully resolve the close similarity between faulty and attack behaviour."

title: "Anomaly-Based Intrusion Detection System in the Internet of Things Using Machine Learning"
authors: Laboni Sarkar; Ranjan Kumar Mondal
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) refers to a new category of computing that links the Internet primarily with tangible items. Belonging to different domains With IoT involvement increasing in modern technological advancements, attacks and anomaly detection are also concerns in the IoT domain. This survey provides a structured and comprehensive anomaly detection algorithm evaluation, a testament to our commitment to resolving IoT security issues. In this paper, we recommend assessing the workings of several machine learning models used in this study to predict attacks and adequately capture anomalies in IoT systems. We choose datasets from the Distributed Smart Space Orchestration System (DS2OS). We chose thirteen well-established algorithms from the sklearn library to build the final Models and compare results. The statistical evaluation metric compares the model’s performance and detects anomalies in the IoT system. The final result of the proposed work is an evaluation of the performance and accuracy of the machine learning models, demonstrating the thoroughness of our research. title: "DarkSegments_IDS"
authors: Mohamed Almaleki
abstract: "AbstractThis dataset presents a comprehensive collection of plaintext and evasive web attack traffic designed to support research in intrusion detection systems (IDS), adversarial robustness, malicious payload analysis, and machine learning-based cybersecurity defenses. The dataset addresses a key limitation of many publicly available intrusion detection datasets, which primarily contain canonical attack representations and lack semantically preserved evasive attack behaviors commonly used by adversaries to bypass modern detection systems.The dataset consists of both network flow-based traffic representations and HTTP payload-level representations for multiple web application attack categories, including SQL Injection (SQLi), Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), and Command Injection (CMDi). Each attack family contains both canonical (plaintext) attack samples and semantically equivalent evasive variants generated through realistic payload obfuscation techniques. The dataset supports two classification granularities: attack family-level classification (Benign, SQLi, XSS, CMDi) and attack variant-level classification, enabling both coarse-grained and fine-grained security analytics.The SQL injection category includes multiple attack variants, including Boolean-based SQL Injection (B_SQLi), Tautology-based SQL Injection (T_SQLi), and Union-based SQL Injection (U_SQLi). Cross-Site Scripting attacks include both standard XSS payloads and event-handler-based XSS variants, while Command Injection (CMDi) samples represent operating system command execution attempts through HTTP requests. Benign traffic is included to simulate legitimate web interactions and provide realistic class separation for classification tasks.To enhance realism and evaluate detection robustness under adversarial conditions, evasive attack samples were generated using semantics-preserving mutation and obfuscation techniques commonly observed in real-world attack scenarios. These techniques include keyword case manipulation, inline comment insertion, syntax fragmentation, encoding transformations, payload restructuring, event-handler mutation, and lexical obfuscation, allowing malicious behavior to remain functionally unchanged while altering its observable representation. Such transformations are specifically designed to challenge detection approaches that rely heavily on static signatures or statistical feature patterns.The dataset is organized into four primary components: (1) plaintext flow traffic, (2) evasive flow traffic, (3) plaintext HTTP payloads, and (4) evasive HTTP payloads. Flow-level representations were generated using CICFlowMeter-compatible statistical features, enabling benchmarking of flow-based intrusion detection models. Payload-level representations preserve HTTP Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) and HTTP payload structures, supporting payload-aware machine learning, natural language-inspired security analysis, feature engineering, and deep learning applications.This dataset enables multiple research directions, including robustness evaluation of IDS against evasive attacks, adversarial machine learning, transferability analysis between plaintext and evasive attack distributions, feature representation comparison, payload-aware intrusion detection, and model generalization assessment under distribution shift conditions. Furthermore, it supports benchmarking of machine learning, deep learning, and adversarially trained models, enabling researchers to evaluate the limitations of flow-based representations and the effectiveness of payload-aware approaches under realistic evasion scenarios.By integrating semantically preserved evasive attack variants with both flow and payload representations, this dataset provides a reproducible and extensible benchmark for evaluating whether cybersecurity detection systems can generalize beyond conventional attack signatures and static feature spaces. The dataset is intended for researchers and practitioners in cybersecurity, intrusion detection, secure artificial intelligence, adversarial robustness, and web application security, facilitating the development of more resilient and explainable defensive systems."

title: "IQ-0 DATASET"
authors: Arihanta Mishra
abstract: "This dataset contains cleaned and processed flow-level network traffic records designed for intelligent cyberattack detection and intrusion detection research. It includes both normal traffic and multiple attack categories such as Brute Force, Port Scan, HTTP DDoS, ICMP Flood, and Web Crawling. The dataset is suitable for binary attack detection, multi-class attack classification, anomaly detection, sequential deep learning, and explainable AI-based analysis. It can be used to benchmark models such as MLP, LSTM, TCN, Autoencoders, and hybrid detection systems. Due to class imbalance across attack types, the dataset is also useful for evaluating robust metrics such as macro-F1, per-class recall, ROC-AUC, and inference latency. This resource supports research on AI-driven cybersecurity, behavioral attack profiling, and analyst-assisted incident response."

title: "Network Performance Monitoring Dataset under Benign and DDoS Attack Traffic"
authors: Md Toufiqur Rahman (9655855); Md Farhad Hossain
abstract: "This dataset contains per-minute network and server performance monitoring logs collected using PRTG Network Monitor from an Apache2 web server hosted on a Raspberry Pi running Ubuntu 22.04 LTS. Two client machines were connected to the server through a router: one generated distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack traffic using the Low Orbit Ion Cannon (LOIC) tool, and the other generated normal (\"benign\") traffic. The dataset covers 31 monitoring sessions (16 benign, 15 attack) totaling 1,860 one-minute readings, capturing CPU load (total and per-core), ping time, packet loss, HTTP loading time, network traffic volume\/speed (in\/out\/total), sensor downtime, ping jitter, and execution time. It was collected to support research on machine-learning-based prediction of network hardware failure and detection of cyberattack-driven anomalies, accompanying the paper \"Next-Gen Network Security: Deep Learning for Predicting Hardware Failures and Cyber Anomaly Detection.\" Note that this dataset itself contains performance-monitoring readings under benign\/attack traffic conditions, not direct hardware-failure event labels \u2014 it is the precursor monitoring signal used for that prediction task. Attack sessions in this release are UDP-flood DDoS traffic; see the included README for full details, column definitions, and known limitations."

title: "OfficeShield-DS: A Behavioral Network Flow Dataset for AI-Enhanced IDS in IoT Camera Environments"
authors: Rayan Nadeem; Sameed  Asif; Abdullah  Farooq
abstract: "This dataset contains 715,581 behavioral network flow records captured on a Raspberry Pi 5 edge device during sequential Denial-of-Service (DoS) attack simulations. Four attack types are included SYN flood, UDP flood, ICMP flood, and HTTP flood along with benign baseline traffic. All attacks were generated using custom Python scripts in a controlled, personally owned environment, ensuring clean labels without privacy concerns.Each flow is represented by 40 behavioral features focusing on packet timing (inter-arrival times), TCP flags, packet size distributions, and traffic concentration metrics, rather than payload contents. The dataset is offered in two forms: (1) a full imbalanced dataset (715,581 records) reflecting real-world attack distributions, and (2) a balanced subset (125,000 records with 25,000 per class) suitable for fair machine learning benchmarking. The edge-captured nature of this data makes it particularly valuable for researchers developing lightweight intrusion detection systems for IoT and resource-constrained environments."

title: "SQL_Injection_Detection_Payloads_V2_Extended"
authors: Md Mehedi Hassan; Rubaeat Ahammed
abstract: "AbstractSQL_Injection_Detection_Payloads_V2_Extended is an extended cybersecurity dataset developed for binary SQL injection intent detection, payload analysis, and defensive machine-learning research. It expands the foundational SQL_Injection_Detection_Payloads dataset by increasing the corpus to 320,000 labeled records, comprising 175,000 malicious SQL injection records and 145,000 benign records. The dataset includes SQL injection payloads, ordinary user inputs, genuine SQL statements, parameterized SQL, structured application requests, security-related text, contextual hard negatives, encoded payloads, and obfuscated attack patterns.The dataset provides broad representation of SQL injection types, taxonomies, payload structures, anatomical components, and exploitation strategies. The covered categories include UNION-based, error-based, Boolean-blind, time-based, stacked-query, authentication-bypass, second-order candidate, query-clause manipulation, subquery injection, metadata enumeration, DBMS fingerprinting, out-of-band interaction, file access, command execution, privilege escalation, encoding, obfuscation, parenthesis breakout, and hybrid chaining patterns. Payload anatomy is modeled through delivery context, injection point, breakout prefix, operator, conditional logic, technique core, attack target, termination mechanism, and encoding or evasion layer.The records cover MySQL, PostgreSQL, Microsoft SQL Server, Oracle, generic SQL, and cross-DBMS-compatible patterns. Inputs are represented through form, raw, HTTP, JSON, XML, GraphQL, Cookie, User-Agent, CSV, and genuine SQL contexts. The dataset contains 61 controlled malicious taxonomy classes, one residual malicious-unclassified category, nine DBMS-family values, ten input contexts, and four encoding categories. Exact duplicates, normalized-template duplicates, and cross-split template-family overlap were reduced to zero under the implemented validation procedure. Prepared training, validation, and test partitions are provided using an 80:10:10 ratio. The dataset is intended for SQL injection classifier development, robustness analysis, false-positive investigation, taxonomy research, comparative evaluation, and authorized web-application security research."

It is offered as an operational tool to improve consistency, traceability, and navigability within the corpus. It is not a physical theory, nor does it assert ontological claims about regimes. This document also serves to strengthen the logical integration between the C* series and the Physmatics Machine Learning Index (PMLI) by making inter-document relationships explicit and machine-interpretable. 2. Core Definitions 2.1 Regime A regime is a coherent interval of recurrence during which a single structural description — consisting of variables, constraints, and applicable dynamical templates — remains sufficient to maintain explanatory coherence under continuous transport and relaxation. 2.2 Regime Crossing A regime crossing is a transition at which no continuous adjustment of parameters within the current structural description can preserve identity and coherence. At such a point, re-indexing becomes necessary. 2.3 Re-indexing Re-indexing is the minimal change to the bookkeeping description (variables, state labels, constraints, or representation basis) required to restore explanatory coherence after a regime crossing. 2.4 Recurrence Index (R) The Recurrence Index (R) is the independent variable along which regimes evolve and are indexed. It serves as the ordering parameter for both continuous dynamical evolution and discrete re-indexing events. 3. Regime Classification Criteria Regime classification provides a consistent, minimal framework for distinguishing one regime from another. Classification is operational and descriptive. It is grounded in observable behavior under the dynamical templates of C5 and the conditions that activate detection under C4. Classification dimensions include, but are not limited to: • Coherence character under constrained transport and relaxation • Dominant constraint type active within the regime • Recurrence behavior as R increases (growth-limited, relaxation-dominated, stable, or transitional) • Sensitivity to transition under stress testing Classification serves bookkeeping, consistency, and traceability. It does not constitute a claim about the physical or ontological nature of regimes. 4. Indexing Protocol 4.1 Trigger for Re-indexing Re-indexing is required only when all three necessary conditions defined in the h³π Detection Protocol (C4) are satisfied. Continuous application of the Transport Invariant (C5) must first be exhausted. 4.2 Minimal Re-indexing Principle When re-indexing is required, the change to the structural description shall be minimal. Only those elements necessary to restore coherence shall be modified. 4.3 Valid Re-indexing Actions Valid re-indexing actions include: • Introduction or change of a regime label • Addition or modification of a constraint class • Change of representation basis • Introduction of a discrete transition variable 4.4 Stability Validation Any proposed re-indexing must demonstrate stability under the stress tests defined in C4 (sensitivity to initialization, parameter sweep, and holdout validation). 4.5 Ledger Syntax Regime indices and transitions shall be recorded using consistent, auditable syntax. title: A 4-Month Dataset of Interactive SSH Honeypot Logs and Command Payloads
authors: Viktor Boiko; Oleksandr Niiakyi
abstract: This article describes a longitudinal dataset of high-interaction SSH honeypot logs collected over a four-month period from July to November 2025. The data was captured using a custom modular multi-threaded honeypot developed in Python 3.10, utilizing the Paramiko library to simulate an interactive SSHv2 environment. Unlike low-interaction systems, this dataset records the full spectrum of adversary activity, including initial connection attempts, authentication brute-forcing, and post-authentication command execution. The resulting dataset contains 145,425 security events, structured to support session reconstruction via unique identifiers. The telemetry includes source IPv4 addresses, credential pairs, and granular command-line payloads, featuring rare instances of file-less exploitation via bash sockets. This data provides a ground-truth source for training machine learning models for anomaly detection, enhancing SIEM rule-sets, and conducting empirical research into botnet orchestration and manual intrusion tactics in cloud infrastructures. This is a preprint of a paper submitted to Data in Brief. This preprint describes the dataset available at DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.19815504 and utilizes the software framework archived at DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.19817625.

title: A 6G Integrated Sensing and Communication Framework for Railway Intrusion Detection and Collision Prediction
authors: Ajeet Kumar Yadav; Sankaran Balasubramaniam; Aritra Chatterjee; Vinod Aduru; Yogesh L. Simmhan; Pandarasamy Arjunan
abstract: Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) combines sensing and communication to efficiently utilize wireless resources and is emerging as a key paradigm for next-generation wireless networks. By leveraging the wide bandwidth, high frequencies, and massive antenna arrays of 5G-Advanced and 6G systems, ISAC enables physical-layer sensing using Channel State Information (CSI). The 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) Release 19 identifies 32 potential ISAC use cases, with particular emphasis on detecting and tracking moving objects. In this work, we address the Sensing for Railway Intrusion Detection use case, where intruders, including wildlife, entering a railway track can pose serious collision risks. We generated 22,695 CSI matrices with corresponding ground truth using a 3D-rendered railway environment and the Sionna radio simulator. We developed a machine learning model combining a three-dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (3D CNN) and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) network to detect intruders in the track danger zone and estimate their real-time position relative to the train, velocity, and time to collision. On synthetic CSI data, the model achieves 99.57% intruder-detection accuracy on a balanced test set and a combined Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.4240 for position, velocity, and time-to-collision prediction. These results demonstrate the potential of CSI-based ISAC sensing with machine learning for reliable railway intrusion detection. The complete codebase for CSI generation, preprocessing, and model development is publicly available at https://github.com/EdgeIntelligenceLab/6g-isac-railway-intrusion-detection.

title: A BERT-Based Natural Language Processing Framework for Detecting Social Engineering and Manipulation Attacks in Digital Communication Channels
authors: Abd Alwahab Maroof
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Social engineering attacks are a growing Cybersecurity threat because they target human psychology instead of technical weaknesses. Attackers use fake urgency, impersonate trusted people, or offer false rewards to trick victims into sharing passwords or sending money. Traditional security tools like spam filters often miss these attacks because they look for malicious links or attachments, not manipulative language. This APR project proposes a system that uses BERT, which is a powerful natural language processing model, to automatically detect social engineering and manipulation attempts in digital messages such as emails, SMS , and chat conversations. The system works by first cleaning and preparing the message text, then passing it through a BERT-based classifier that has been fine-tuned on labeled phishing and social engineering datasets. Finally, it outputs a prediction and generates an alert if an attack is detected. Based on results from similar research studies, the BERT model is expected to achieve around 94-95% accuracy in detecting social engineering attacks, which is significantly better than traditional machine learning methods like SVM or Random Forest. The system also provides a simple dashboard for users to monitor threats and review past detections. The main contribution of this project is a practical NLP-based detection framework that can be integrated into email clients or messaging apps to protect users from psychological manipulation attacks. The results show that transformer-based models like BERT are well-suited for this task because they understand context and subtle language cues that rule-based systems cannot. This work was conducted at Arab International University (AIU), Syria. The official website of the university is: https://www.aiu.edu.sy

title: A Comparative Evaluation of Unsupervised Anomaly Detection Techniques for Secure IoT Traffic Analysis
authors: Badriya Murdhi Alenzi; Nasser Allheeib; Sultan Alamri
abstract: Internet of things (IoT) is an important technology that has numerous applications in many industries. Since IoT involves sensing of data and communication of this data between IoT nodes and IoT sensors, it is vulnerable to cyberattacks from malicious users. Anomaly detection is an important cybersecurity technique that can help identify abnormal data traffic patterns. In this work, a comparative evaluation of unsupervised anomaly detection techniques using feature reduction is presented for IoT traffic analysis. A realistic IoT attacks dataset developed by the Canadian Institute for Cybersecurity is used in this regard. The attacks considered in this dataset include denial of service HTTP flooding attacks. We utilize four machine learning techniques, namely, isolation forest, local outlier factor (LOF), one‐class support vector machine (one‐class SVM), and elliptic envelope on the considered dataset. Extensive simulation results show that one‐class SVM has the best performance in terms of recall and F1 score. On the other hand, isolation forest shows the balanced performance for all the considered metrics.

title: A Comparative Review of Real-Time Intrusion Detection Systems for Sustainable and Connected Cyber Infrastructures
authors: Emmanuel Innocent Umoh; Hussaini Bishara; Amrita; Jayant Jha
venue: 2026 International Conference on Sustainable Engineering and Technology Innovations (ICSETI)
abstract: The components of real-time intrusion detection and prevention systems (RT-IDPS) is review systematically in this paper. Specifically, with a focus on the system’s architectures, detection methodologies, contexts of application, and their limitations. To achieve this, a structured review approach is used, resulting in the analysis of 30 peer-reviewed studies that were recently published between the years 2018 and 2025 in various research databases, including but not limited to IEEE Xplore, ACM, Springer, and ScienceDirect. The reviewed literature is classified into three major categories, namely, signature-based, anomaly-based and hybrid approaches, with a direct focus on the use of advanced deep and reinforcement learning approaches. The comparative analysis was conducted based on a number of key parameters, which include detection accuracy, false positive rate, scalability, and applicability of datasets. The analysis showed that while hybrid and deep learning models give significantly advanced detection capabilities, they continue to struggle with key issues of handling encrypted data traffic, scalability, and the ability to generalize. In relation to these identified gaps, this paper established four proposed directions: federated adaptive learning, multistage lightweight processing pipelines, encrypted traffic behavioural modelling, and real-time threat intelligence fusion. This review highlights a new framework for the RT-IDPS to work toward in alignment with the sustainable digital practice to reduce system downtime, minimize energy intensive recovery process. Hereby, sustainability-aware RT-IDS design improves long-term operational efficiency and provides a resilient, adaptive security system for sustainable, intelligent, connected cyber infrastructure.

title: A Comparison of SSL-Based Feature Extractors and Back-End Classifiers for Spoofing Detection: A Multi-Corpus Training and Cross-Linguistic Analysis
authors: Anh-Tuan Dao; D. Matrouf; Mickael Rouvier; Nicholas W. D. Evans
venue: The Speaker and Language Recognition Workshop
abstract: Voice biometric systems face growing threats from spoofing attacks, yet the evaluation of detection models remains inconsistent across datasets. To investigate these unpredictable fluctuations, we conduct a comprehensive benchmark of four self-supervised learning feature extractors paired with four back-end classifiers. We compare the hierarchical local feature extraction of ResNet with the global sequence and relational modeling of attention and graph-based back-ends. Through multi-corpus training across three scenarios and six evaluation datasets, our empirical analysis yields two critical findings. First, we expose a domain bias within the ASVspoof 5 dataset, showing that naive data scaling actively degrades performance. Second, our cross-linguistic analysis reveals that fine-tuning with just 8 hours of target-language data enhances detection robustness. Together, these findings emphasize the critical need for domain-aware and language-specific adaptation in spoofing detection.

title: A Comprehensive Analysis of Intrusion Detection Systems Across Cloud, IoT, and Cyber-Physical Environments
authors: Shelley Gupta; Mohit Jain; Tanya Chaudhary; Harikesh Singh
venue: 2026 International Conference on Intelligent Systems in Engineering, Secured Systems and Cybersecurity (ICISESSC)
abstract: Today, the concept of an Intrusion Detection System (IDS) is vital when it comes to safeguarding the information infrastructures of modern computer systems from complex cyberattack methods. The rise of cloud computing, the internet of things, and cyber-physical systems has produced more different types of attack surfaces than ever before. This leads to an IDS that scale up and down, adapt inexpensively or even for free, and can work within heterogeneous environments. The paper evaluates an emerging type of IDS, multi-level intrusion detection systems, being specifically developed for Cloud-based and distributed systems. Each of the four techniques used to identify fraud in a client-initiated transaction will be applied in this project in terms of their effectiveness and efficiency (Signature, Anomaly, Behavior, Hybrid) while also noting how machine learning, deep learning, and AI techniques apply to these methods. Comparative performances on the most widely used benchmark datasets show that by implementing Hybrid or Multi-Level IDS architectures, companies can obtain better detection accuracy while achieving lower false positives and less operational overhead compared to traditional IDS architectures. The paper reviews existing research, identifies remaining challenges in the field of IDS, and outlines a framework for future IDS research and development through an overview of challenges faced by IDS such as encrypted traffic, scalability, detection in real time, and energy constrained environments.

title: A Comprehensive Literature Survey on Hybrid Deep Learning Approaches for Network Intrusion Detection
authors: Vishwa K. Patel; Premal C. Patel; Satvik V. Khara
venue: 2026 International Conference on AI-Driven Smart Systems and Ubiquitous Computing (ICAUC)
abstract: Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) play a critical role in securing modern network infrastructures against increasingly sophisticated cyberattacks. Traditional machine learning–based IDS often struggle to achieve robust detection performance due to issues such as class imbalance, evolving attack patterns, encrypted network traffic and limited generalization across datasets. To address these challenges, hybrid deep learning–based IDS models have emerged as a promising solution by combining complementary learning architectures to enhance detection accuracy and adaptability. This paper presents a comprehensive survey of hybrid deep learning approaches for network intrusion detection, systematically categorizing existing models based on their architectural design, learning strategies, datasets and evaluation metrics. The study analyzes the effectiveness of hybrid models in handling class imbalance, feature representatio and cross-dataset generalization, while highlighting their limitations in real-world deployment scenarios. Furthermore, the paper identifies critical research gaps related to encrypted traffic analysis, scalability and explainability and maps these gaps to potential future research directions. By providing a structured taxonomy and critical analysis, this survey offers valuable insights for researchers and practitioners aiming to design efficient, robust and deployable hybrid IDS solutions.

title: A Comprehensive Review of Cybersecurity Frameworks and Defense Mechanisms for Modbus and HTTP in Industrial Control Systems
authors: Lukumba Phiri; Mukubesa Kamutumwa
venue: International Journal of Applied Mathematics Computational Science and Systems Engineering
abstract: Industrial Control Systems (ICS) form the backbone of critical infrastructure, enabling automation and control in sectors such as energy, water, and manufacturing. The convergence of Operational Technology (OT) and Information Technology (IT) has introduced significant cybersecurity challenges, particularly for legacy communication protocols like Modbus and HTTP, which were not designed with security in mind. This paper provides a comprehensive framework for understanding the attack and defense mechanisms associated with two protocols i.e., Modbus and HTTP, used in ICS. We systematically analyze the inherent vulnerabilities of these protocols, survey proposed security enhancements including cryptographic solutions, intrusion detection systems, and security-by-design approaches, and evaluate existing cybersecurity frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK, NIST CSF, and the Cyber Kill Chain. The review identifies a persistent gap in integrated, protocol-specific frameworks that address both attack simulation and defense validation in virtualized ICS environments. By synthesizing current research, this study highlights trends in threat modeling, machine learning-based anomaly detection, and the evolution of testbeds, providing a foundation for future work aimed at developing holistic security frameworks for Modbus and HTTP-based industrial networks.

title: A Comprehensive Review of Quantum Scrambling as a Cryptographic Resource in Quantum Key Distribution
authors: Syed Muntasir Mamun
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This review examines the preprint by Daniel Süß titled "Quantum Scrambling as a Cryptographic Resource: From Krylov Complexity to Physical Channel Authentication," which proposes quantum scrambling in many-body quantum channels as a novel cryptographic primitive for channel authentication in quantum key distribution (QKD). Key postulates include the irreversibility of scrambling dynamics, the role of Lanczos coefficients in determining channel autocorrelation signatures, and the practical unforgeability protected by doubly exponential Poincaré recurrence times. Hypotheses center on the deterministic, measurable, and secure nature of scrambling-derived fingerprints, validated through simulations and real astrophysical data from the NANOGrav dataset. Results demonstrate high detection accuracy (AUC = 0.99) under realistic noise. Similar research in quantum chaos, Krylov complexity, and QKD security is surveyed, highlighting ongoing trends toward physics-based cryptography amid quantum threats. Algebraic interpretations frame Krylov subspaces as orthogonal bases for operator evolution, while geometric views depict scrambling as diffusive spreading in operator space. The field is advancing toward hybrid quantum-classical protocols resilient to quantum attacks, potentially revolutionizing secure communications. title: A Comprehensive Survey of Acceleration Techniques for Intrusion Detection and Prevention Systems: Taxonomy, Architectures, Challenges, and Future Trends
authors: Samia Choueiri; Sergio Elizalde; Ali AlSabeh; Amith GSPN; Ali Mazloum; Jose Gomez et al.

title: A Comprehensive Survey on Machine Learning and Deep Learning Approaches for Network Intrusion Detection Systems: Techniques, Datasets, and Open Challenges
authors: Yahya Alnattaf; Hanaa Mahmood
abstract: The rapid expansion of networked infrastructure, cloud computing, and IoT environments has significantly increased the attack surface, while traditional signature-based Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDS) remain limited in detecting zero-day attacks, polymorphic threats, and malicious activities within encrypted traffic. This survey reviews and synthesizes a decade of research from 2015 to 2025 on Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) approaches for NIDS, providing a unified taxonomy that organizes existing methods according to both their learning paradigms, including supervised, unsupervised, semi-supervised, reinforcement, and self-supervised learning, and their architectural designs, such as classical ML, convolutional, recurrent, autoencoder, generative, attention-based, transformer, graph, and federated models. The review shows that tree-based ensemble methods, particularly Random Forest and XGBoost, continue to provide strong and competitive baselines for tabular network-flow data, highlighting the need for more complex DL models to demonstrate clear practical advantages. Hybrid spatio-temporal architectures, such as CNN-LSTM models, and transformer-based approaches have achieved strong performance on recent datasets; however, results on saturated benchmarks such as NSL-KDD provide limited evidence of meaningful progress. More importantly, cross-dataset evaluations reveal substantial generalization gaps, with F1-score differences of approximately 20–30 percentage points, indicating persistent problems related to dataset bias and label quality. Overall, NIDS research is gradually moving beyond the pursuit of higher accuracy toward practical challenges such as real-time edge inference, adversarial robustness, explainability, privacy-preserving and federated learning, and intrusion detection over encrypted traffic. Based on these findings, this survey highlights standardized feature representations, rigorous temporal and cross-dataset evaluation, and self-supervised pre-training as promising directions for developing more robust and generalizable NIDS models.

title: A Comprehensive Systematic Review of AI-based Network Intrusion Detection Systems: Techniques, Datasets, Challenges, and Future Research Directions
authors: Mehdi Gheisari; Zhou Pingmei; Basheer Riskhan; Malusi Sibiya; Faizan Khan Muhammad; Seyed Kazem Gheblezadeh
venue: Journal of Computing and Data Technology
abstract: The rapid expansion of cloud computing platforms, Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystems, edge devices, software-defined networks, and distributed enterprise infrastructures has significantly increased the complexity and scale of modern cybersecurity environments. Traditional signature-based intrusion detection systems are increasingly ineffective against sophisticated cyber threats such as zero-day attacks, advanced persistent threats, ransomware propagation, botnet activities, and encrypted malicious traffic because they rely heavily on predefined attack signatures and static rule-based detection mechanisms. Consequently, AI driven intrusion detection systems have emerged as promising solutions for intelligent threat detection, adaptive cybersecurity analytics, and real-time network defense. This paper presents a comprehensive systematic literature review of AI based network intrusion detection systems with particular emphasis on machine learning, deep learning, federated learning, and intelligent anomaly detection frameworks. Furthermore, the study evaluates benchmark cybersecurity datasets including NSL-KDD, CICIDS2017, UNSW-NB15, DARPA, and TON-IoT datasets to investigate their effectiveness, scalability, realism, and applicability for modern intrusion detection research. Comparative analysis indicates that deep learning and hybrid AI techniques significantly improve intrusion detection accuracy, adaptive threat detection, and real-time cybersecurity analytics compared with traditional approaches. The paper further discusses major challenges including adversarial attacks, encrypted traffic analysis, dataset imbalance, explainability, computational overhead, and concept drift. Emerging research directions such as federated intrusion detection, Transformer-based cybersecurity, graph neural networks, self-supervised learning, and explainable AI are also critically analyzed.

title: A constructive graph model for handling the industrial threats using learning approaches
authors: Ashwini D. Gulhane; A. K. Velmurugan
abstract: The industrial internet of things (IIoT) has reshaped Industry 4.0 by enabling large-scale connectivity among intelligent devices and supporting new levels of digital automation and analytics. However, the distributed nature of IIoT, together with Industrial 5G connectivity, heterogeneous sensing devices, IT/OT convergence, edge computing, and time-sensitive networking, significantly expands the attack surface. In particular, complex multi-variant persistent botnet attacks pose a severe threat to operational continuity and safety. Early and accurate detection of such attacks remains challenging due to evolving behaviors, encrypted traffic, and the limitations of signature-based detection. To address this problem, this paper proposes a hybrid deep learning-enabled approach called the graph constructive localization model (GCLM) to defend IIoT infrastructure against sophisticated botnet attacks. GCLM converts traffic sequences into graphs, learns node embeddings using Word2Vec, extracts high-level representations through graph convolution, and improves interpretability and discriminability using global attention pooling and supervised contrastive learning. The proposed model is evaluated using recent benchmark methodologies, conventional and extended performance metrics, and widely used intrusion datasets. Experimental results show that GCLM achieves a 99.9% botnet detection rate and an average detection time of 0.066[Formula: see text]ms, outperforming existing deep learning and hybrid baselines in both accuracy and efficiency.

title: A Data-Centric Network Traffic Dataset for Anomaly Detection: Construction, Reproducible Pipeline, and Technical Validation
authors: Daniel Quirumbay Yagual; Diego Fernández; Francisco Javier Novoa; D. Garabato
abstract: The effectiveness of machine learning and deep learning methods for network anomaly detection depends strongly on the quality and representativeness of the datasets used for training and evaluation. Despite recent advances, many publicly available benchmarks rely on synthetic traffic, outdated attack scenarios, or limited representation of encrypted communications. This work presents a network traffic dataset derived from operational firewall logs collected in a heterogeneous institutional environment dominated by HTTPS/TLS traffic. A structured data-centric pipeline was implemented, including preprocessing, behavioral feature engineering, unsupervised pseudo-labeling through the EFMS–KMeans algorithm, class balancing using SMOTE, and the generation of model-oriented sequential representations for deep learning analysis. The resulting dataset contains large-scale flow-level records describing volumetric, behavioral, and temporal traffic characteristics while preserving privacy through anonymization procedures. Technical validation was conducted using statistical analysis, entropy-based measurements, clustering quality metrics, and dimensionality reduction techniques, confirming data consistency, structural diversity, and class separability. The dataset is publicly available through the Mendeley Data repository together with metadata and documentation supporting anomaly detection research, encrypted traffic analysis, and the evaluation of machine learning and deep learning approaches in realistic cybersecurity environments.

title: A Dataset and Service for Automated Identification of Security Bug Reports
authors: Horácio L. França; César Teixeira; Nuno Laranjeiro
abstract: Reporting the presence of a security bug allows developers to take action and correct security vulnerabilities before they can be exploited by attackers. The analysis of a security bug report is mostly a manual activity, which, among many other tasks, requires the effort and time of one or more developers to check if the reported issue is actually an issue or not. Several studies have tried to automate report identification using machine learning, but given that vulnerabilities are infrequent bugs, models do not really perform well, especially due to the fact that it is difficult to collect sufficient and diverse data for training. We aim to contribute a large and diverse dataset to aid in security report identification. In this work, we gather security bug reports that are diverse and were collected from heterogeneous sources to form a security bug report dataset. The main goal is to support research that aims at automating the identification and classification of security bug reports. We provide our dataset, as well as a few pre-trained machine learning models, as a publicly available REpresentational State Transfer (REST) service that enables communication between applications over HTTP).We also illustrate the usefulness of our dataset with a set of typical machine learning experiments, which resulted in models achieving an f-score of 67.5% (relatedwork on similar datasets reports average f-scores ranging between 38% and 66.5%), while especially focusing on different aspects, such as understanding which content to use for model training or whichwords are more important in the classification process. The work presented here resulted in a dataset to be used in security bug report identification that is larger, with 206,728 reports, and more heterogeneous, with 9 projects, than those observed in related work. Our case studies show their usefulness and highlight typical concerns regarding the use of models to classify bug reports.

title: A dataset-centric review of IoT and IIoT intrusion detection: realism, evaluation biases, and future research directions
authors: D Harsha Vardhan Reddy; Kakelli Anil Kumar
abstract: The rapid growth of IoT and IIoT expands the cyber-attack surface of interconnected and safety-critical systems, and, as such, IDSs have become a fundamental security mechanism. Although very impressive results have been reported for machine learning and deep learning-based IDS in benchmark datasets, these gains often do not generalize to real-world deployments owing to dataset design limitations, realism deficits, and evaluation biases, rather than inherent flaws in detection algorithms, which can lead to significant vulnerabilities in actual operational environments. This study presents a dataset-centric review of widely used intrusion detection datasets from the IIoT, IoT, and traditional network domains. A unified taxonomy differentiates datasets based on the domain context, traffic representation, protocol semantics, and attack modeling assumptions. Based on a common analytical framework, each dataset was reviewed regarding its realism, coverage of the threats, class imbalance, temporal continuity, and modern ML/DL-based evaluation of the IDS. The cross-dataset analysis conducted in this study shows that, in addition to the fact that model architecture and feature engineering play a major role, several studies indicate that the simplicity of the datasets, the class imbalance, and the repetitive attack patterns as well as the evaluation methods can affect accuracy of the IDS. This work further underlines the remaining gaps, such as zero-day and adaptive attacks, limited encrypted traffic, weak temporal evolution, poor support for federated learning, and sparse annotations for explainable IDSs. Finally, this study presents future directions for dataset design aligned with the requirements of next-generation IDSs by highlighting digital twin-based IIoT environments, edge-cloud collaborative data generation, sequential traffic modeling, and explainability-oriented annotations that can ensure robust, trustworthy, and deployment-ready IDS solutions.

title: A Deep Learning Approach for Detecting Social Engineering Attack
authors: Aung Phyo; La Wynn Sandi
abstract: Social engineering (SE) remains a premier vector for data breaches. We present SEABERT, a lightweight 3-layer dual-headed DistilBERT model optimized for real-time detection. Unlike binary filters, SEABERT performs joint binary and 7 - class categorization. Using a diverse corpus of over$\mathbf{7 0 0, 0 0 0}$sam- ples, our$\mathbf{3 2} \boldsymbol{\%}$smaller student model achieved 94.18% multi-class accuracy and a 0.9006 Macro F1-score, outperforming the 6-layer teacher baseline (92.40%). On an NVIDIA RTX 3090, SEABERT achieved a 59% reduction in inference latency ($0.231 ~\text{ms} / \text{sample}$). We further validate robustness against AI-generated lures using predictive entropy thresholding$(\tau)>1.6)$. Source code: https://github.com/Mohammadameen/SEABERT-Detection.

title: A Deep Learning Approach to Detect Phishing Website
authors: Prof.  M.  A.  Tamboli; Prof.  M.  S.  Kale; S. B. Khedkar; Rashmi Jagtap; S.  V.  Wable; S.  B.  Nagare
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Phishing remains one of the most prevalent cybersecu-rity threats, with attackers registering new fraudulent domains that bypass traditional blacklist-based detection systems. This project de-velops a Django web application that uses SVM and CNN classifiers to detect phishing URLs in real time without depending on prior knowledge of specific phishing domains. The system processes URL-level features including length, special characters, domain age, and HTTPS presence extracted from a labeled dataset of phishing and legitimate URLs. Experimental evaluation confirmed that the CNN model outperformed the SVM across all four evaluation metrics, demonstrating the advantage of learning structural URL patterns directly over relying on term frequency weights. The application provides users with instant URL safety predictions, offering a prac-tical phishing detection tool for everyday use across individuals, businesses, and educational institutions.

title: A Deep Learning-Based Approach to Intelligent Web Vulnerability Discovery and Risk Assessment
authors: Hari Aravind Kishore A; Harry Herald R; Lekshmi S. Raveendran
venue: 2026 1st International Conference on Emerging Trends in Advancements and Applications of Computational Intelligence Techniques (ETAACT)
abstract: The fast growth of modern web applications has made them more vulnerable to complex and new types of vulnerabilities, which in turn has exposed the drawbacks of traditional scanners that perform static crawling and depend on signature-based detection. To go beyond the capacity of traditional scanning workflows, we introduce a learner-driven system that not only detects web vulnerabilities but also analyzes the risks brought by them. The core of our solution is a combination of the Open Web Application Security Project Zed Attack Proxy (OWASP ZAP) and a Deep Q-Network (DQN) crawler that dynamically identifies security-critical application paths, a Light Gradient-Boosting Machine (LightGBM) classifier that focuses on prioritizing risks from the point of view of exploitability, and a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)-based autoencoder that identifies anomalous Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) patterns. Results from experimentation indicate that our method is significantly better than a simple signature-based scanning method in terms of reducing false positives, improving prioritization accuracy and extending scan coverage. An analytical look into Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) shows how they can be used in creating adaptive payloads and finding zero-day vulnerabilities. The findings indicate that the use of deep learning (DL), ensemble learning, and reinforcement learning (RL) together leads to a major increase in the capability levels and effectiveness of contemporary web vulnerability assessment systems.

title: A deep reinforcement based echo state network for network intrusion classification
authors: Khorshed Alam; Mahbubul Haq Bhuiyan; Dewan Md. Farid
abstract: Network intrusion classification referred to the process of monitoring and analyzing network traffic to identify suspicious activities or attacks. In this work, author proposed a novel approach to classify network intrusion by utilizing deep reinforcement learning (DRL), integrating a reservoir computing approach Echo State Network (ESN). A DRL-based approach improved upon traditional deep learning by adapting dynamically to novel/unknown and evolving attack patterns. Unlike static models, DRL continuously learned optimal strategies through interaction with the environment, allowing for better detection of previously unseen threats in real-time. To address the class imbalance often encountered in network intrusion datasets, we evaluated the performance of several advanced data balancing techniques, including Borderline-SMOTE, SMOTE-ENN, ADYSN, and K-means SMOTE. The findings demonstrated that the K-means-based data balancing method outperformed other techniques, resulting in the most robust performance across various metrics. Author conducted multi-dataset validation on benchmark datasets like NF-BoT-IoT, NF-UNSW-NB15, NF-ToN-IoT, NF-ToN-IoT-v2, NF-CSE-CIC-IDS2018 and NF-UNSW-NB15-v3 to ensure robustness across different network flow data. For adaptive modeling testing, author excluded some attack types from training data and included them in testing data (e.g., DoS, Backdoor attacks were excluded from the training data but included in the testing data (see Table 3)). The proposed approach enhanced the accuracy and reliability of intrusion detection, making it a viable solution for securing modern network infrastructures. The source code of this work is available in this Github repository (https://github.com/codewithkhurshed/DRLZDNIDS).

title: A Deep Reinforcement Learning–Based Adaptive Framework for Early DDoS Attack Detection and Prevention in Heterogeneous Networks
authors: Sujit Sutradhar; Joy Lal Sarkar; Abhijit Biswas
venue: Journal of Data Science and Intelligent Systems
abstract: Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) attacks are constantly growing in scale, intensity, and attack plan strategies, which are causing significant threats to the heterogeneous network environments, including Internet of Things, edge, cloud, Software-Defined Networks, and 5G networks. This paper presents an adaptive framework of deep reinforcement learning (DRL) in early-stage detection and proactive mitigation of DDoS attacks. The proposed DRL agent operates in active network environments to develop policies through online learning. This helps it address new and unexpected attack patterns. Traditional machine learning and deep learning models depend on unchanging training methods, which run their training process from a fixed point in time. The framework combines the flow-level feature analysis and the packet-level feature analysis with the Deep Q-Network–based learning mechanism to facilitate real-time decision-making. Numerous experiments were carried out on benchmark datasets and heterogeneous traffic simulations. This indicates that the suggested methodology can be considered stable and offers an approximation of 98% accuracy, 96% precision, 96% recall, and 96% macro F1-score on the datasets with up to 300,000 network flows. Further flow analysis shows that flow duration, packet-level variability, and distribution of destination ports are critical in differentiating between benign and malicious traffic. The findings prove that the developed framework can offer detection and mitigation of DDoS threats, which are scalable, robust, and adaptive, to facilitate the creation of intelligent and self-educating cybersecurity systems in complex network settings. Data Availability Statement The datasets used in this study, including CICDDoS2019, NSL-KDD, and UNSW-NB15, are publicly available through their respective repositories. The implementation details, preprocessing procedures, model configurations, and experimental settings are described within the manuscript to facilitate reproducibility. The source code and trained model configurations are available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request and will be considered for public repository release in future work to further enhance research transparency and reproducibility or can be accessed at https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/dhoogla/cicddos2019, https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/hassan06/nslkdd, and https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/mrwellsdavid/unswnb15. title: A deployment-efficient CNN-LSTM framework for real-time malicious traffic detection across heterogeneous, imbalanced, and encrypted network traffic
authors: Marzieh Ghavidel
abstract: Modern enterprise networks, including those adopting Software-Defined Wide Area Network (SD-WAN) architectures, face increasing intrusion detection challenges due to encrypted, heterogeneous, and imbalanced traffic. This paper presents a deployment-aware and robustness-oriented intrusion detection framework motivated by the security requirements of enterprise WAN and SD-WAN deployment environments. The experimental evaluation uses three heterogeneous benchmark traffic domains that are relevant to enterprise WAN monitoring but are not SD-WAN-specific datasets, and that do not cover all operational conditions. The study evaluates a deployment-efficient hybrid CNN-LSTM model across three heterogeneous traffic domains, including laboratory-generated traffic (CICIDS-2017), highly imbalanced multi-attack traffic (UNSW-NB15), and real-world encrypted traffic (CERNET-2020, with a substantial proportion of TLS/SSL-encrypted flows). A lightweight Channel Attention mechanism is incorporated, intended to enhance feature discrimination. SD-WAN is treated strictly as an intended deployment context rather than a validated setting: no SD-WAN testbed or SD-WAN traffic was used. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves 98.1% accuracy, 97.6% F1-score, and 0.99 AUC on the encrypted CERNET dataset, and 99.2% accuracy on CICIDS-2017, achieving strong within-dataset detection performance and providing cross-domain transferability insights across three heterogeneous benchmark datasets. To evaluate cross-domain robustness, a shared-feature transfer setting is introduced between CICIDS-2017 and UNSW-NB15, where the model achieves over 80% accuracy without retraining, indicating partial cross-dataset transferability for this 22-feature aligned subset only. A constrained transferability probe on CERNET (10 shared features only) indicates non-trivial discriminative capability despite substantial feature-space heterogeneity. In addition, the framework is designed for CPU-only inference, with an amortized per-flow model-inference latency of 2.3 ms (batch size 64; traffic acquisition, feature extraction, and window construction excluded), which is not end-to-end detection latency. Overall, this work contributes a systematic robustness evaluation framework for intrusion detection in heterogeneous, encrypted, and imbalanced network environments, addressing the gap between laboratory research and practical enterprise WAN deployment. The CNN-LSTM with channel attention is an established combination; the contribution lies in the evaluation protocol rather than in a new architecture. Comparisons are limited to the baselines evaluated (DNN-LSTM-GRU, PSO-D-SEM, DRL-DQN, and classical machine learning; PSO-D-SEM and DRL-DQN on CERNET only); no Transformer or TCN baseline was included, and no superiority over current methods is claimed. All experiments address the binary task (benign versus malicious); fine-grained attack-family and attack-stage information, which supports threat attribution, response prioritization, and forensics, is not assessed and is lost under this formulation.

title: A Dual-Module Machine Learning Framework for Vulnerability Assessment of Government Payment Gateways: Static Prioritisation and Runtime Detection
authors: Maneno Sudayi; Stephen Manko Wambura; Gaudence Tesha; Christian Budoya
venue: East African Journal of Information Technology
abstract: Government electronic payment gateways concentrate public revenue and citizen data, making them high-value targets whose compromise carries national-security consequences. Yet vulnerability assessment in many public institutions remains manual, severity-driven, and unable to scale against both the growing volume of disclosed weaknesses and the continuous stream of live attack traffic. To address both vulnerability surfaces within a single coherent assessment layer, this paper presents a dual-module machine learning framework that unifies static prioritisation of disclosed vulnerabilities with runtime detection of malicious traffic. Methodologically, the static module prioritises disclosed vulnerabilities by pairing Term Frequency–Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) text representation with Bayesian-optimised XGBoost multi-class classification over a corpus of 386,337 records, built by expanding National Vulnerability Database (NVD) records across their affected libraries using Open Source Vulnerabilities (OSV) data; the runtime module detects malicious HTTP requests using twelve engineered request features and Bayesian-optimised XGBoost binary classification on the CSIC 2010 dataset of 61,065 requests. On the key results, the static module attains a test accuracy of 0.8630, a macro-averaged F1-score of 0.8475, and High-tier recall of 0.9356; the runtime module attains an accuracy of 0.9101, an F1-score of 0.8879, and a ROC-AUC of 0.9796, raising attack recall from 0.087 under a rule-based signature baseline to 0.868. These results demonstrate that interpretable, low-cost learning models can strengthen vulnerability assessment for government payment infrastructure in resource-constrained settings, contributing the first data-driven, reproducible vulnerability-assessment model developed specifically for the Tanzanian Government Electronic Payment Gateway (GePG) context. As principal limitations, we identify the proxy-label limitation, on which the static module is trained against library-exposure breadth rather than a severity or exploitation measure, and the need for institution-specific validation on live GePG traffic, which together define the principal paths for refinement.

title: A Five-Run Comparison of Lightweight Machine Learning Models for IoT Intrusion Detection
authors: Pradyumn Singh; R. Alizadeh
venue: International Journal of Secondary Computing and Applications Research
abstract: IoT intrusion-detection models are useful only if they detect attacks without becoming too costly to run. We compared Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and XGBoost on binary CICIoT2023 intrusion detection using a cleaned file with 21,005,260 rows and 37 numeric features. The main experiment used five attack-resampling balanced outer runs: each outer run reused all 1,047,367 benign records and sampled an equal number of attack records, followed by five inner train-validation-test splits. XGBoost had the highest default-threshold F1-score in the main experiment (0.983109 ± 0.000205), followed by Decision Tree (0.982860 ± 0.000257), Random Forest (0.982237 ± 0.000371), and Logistic Regression (0.974215 ± 0.000272). Because the main outer runs share the benign records, we interpret the paired tests as evidence from repeated attack resampling rather than as five fully independent datasets. To address this limitation, we added a disjoint sensitivity analysis in which both benign and attack rows were resampled into non-overlapping 100,000-per-class outer subsets. The same general pattern remained: XGBoost reached 0.982572 ± 0.000612 F1, while Logistic Regression reached 0.974407 ± 0.000920. A feature-ablation check dropping Number and HTTPS caused only small F1 decreases and did not change the main ordering. Per-record inference latency on the main balanced test split ranged from 0.615 μs for Logistic Regression to 1.124 μs for Random Forest, with XGBoost at 0.647 μs. Overall, the results support tree-based models for this controlled binary benchmark, while also showing why latency, footprint, and dataset-specific shortcuts must be considered before making deployment claims.

title: A Framework for Detecting Application Layer DDOS Attacks in SDN Using Artificial Intelligence
authors: Sarabjeet Kaur; Jasvir Singh Kalsi
venue: International Conference on Computing for Sustainable Global Development
abstract: The researchers strive to secure the infrastructure layer or protect the controller, but forget the application, which can be subjected to DDoS (Distributed Denial of Service). Moreover, since the benchmark dataset of AL-DDoS (Application Layer DDoS) attacks does not exist, researchers resort to using outdated or otherwise irrelevant datasets, and synthetic data is the most popular. The present research is set to concentrate on finding the AL-DDoS attacks within SDN (Software Defined Networking) networks, detecting the features to be analyzed, and using different machine-learning methods to validate the findings. The proposed research identifies key user-behavior attributes that help detect DDoS attack traffic at the application layer in Software-Defined Networking (SDN) environments. Using the SDN-based ‘Slow Read Dataset,’ the study highlights a set of features associated with HTTP flood DDoS attacks. It also reviews features commonly adopted by researchers in existing literature, focusing on differences in browsing behavior between legitimate users and attackers. To demonstrate the effectiveness of these selected features in the detection process, the work applies dimensionality-reduction techniques which minimize the feature set and generate a lower-dimensional dataset for further analysis.

title: A framework for phishing and web attack detection using ensemble features of self-supervised pre-trained models
authors: Paul Ntim Yeboah; A. S. M. Kayes; Wenny J. Rahayu; Eric Pardede; Syed Mahbub
venue: Journal of Network and Computer Applications
abstract: Cyber-attacks on industrial applications, specifically, phishing and web attacks are the most common data breach vectors and, as such, have attracted significant research attention. To mitigate these types of attacks, many countermeasures based on machine learning (ML) have been proposed. Although MLbased countermeasures are reported to yield satisfactory detection performance on phishing and web attacks, they often require massive amounts of manually labelled email and web request data to build these countermeasures. The manual generation of labels, however, can be laborious, error-prone, and may not be proactive in detecting novel phishing schemes and web attacks since attacks need to be identified and annotated prior to training. To cope with the evolution of web attacks and phishing emails, methods which exploit the vast volumes of unlabelled email and web request data should be adopted. This study therefore proposes self-supervised learning (SSL) based on computer vision (CV) and natural language processing (NLP) techniques to pre-train models on unlabelled email texts and HTTP web requests for the detection of phishing emails and web attacks. By leveraging NLP and CV SSL methods, we pre-train models to learn the structural and contextual representations of unlabelled email texts and HTTP requests. By ensembling the features extracted from the pre-trained models, we obtain robust representations of email text and HTTP request data for the effective detection of phishing emails and web attacks. The experiment results on an imbalanced dataset show that the combined self-supervised pre-trained models outperform other existing works in respect to accuracy, precision, recall and F1-score for phishing email and web attack detection.

title: A Generalized Video Platform Identification Method Over Obfuscated Encrypted Protocols in Real-World Networks
authors: Qing Chen; Hua Wu; Tian Tian; Anting Lu; Guang Cheng; Xiao-Yan Hu
venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
abstract: Despite platforms adopt encryption protocols such as TLS to protect user privacy, adversaries can still infer user preferences through platform identification attacks. To obtain enhanced privacy, a lot of users employ obfuscated encrypted protocols, such as encrypted proxies and virtual private networks. However, existing state-of-the-art platform identification methods are only effective in laboratory-closed networks. In real-world networks, their performance degrades significantly when confronted with unknown obfuscated encrypted protocols or dynamic transmission paths. In addition, asymmetric routing also substantially weakens their effectiveness, which is a prevalent scenario in real-world networks. To overcome these challenges, this paper introduces a generalized method for identifying encrypted video streams over obfuscated encrypted protocols. Our approach achieves this by designing protocol-agnostic and path-agnostic features through granular analysis of video transmission patterns. Specifically, we first extract the inherent transmission patterns from unidirectional flows. Subsequently, we derive robust statistical features from temporal and spatial dimensions, respectively. Finally, these features are used to train a machine-learning-based classifier. Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a classification accuracy exceeding 98% against both unknown obfuscated encrypted protocols and dynamic transmission paths. Compared with the state-of-the-art methods, our method requires only 15% of the storage and 74% of the computational time while delivering superior performance. These findings reveal significant privacy vulnerabilities in obfuscated encrypted protocols and underscore the urgent need for developing more advanced security mechanisms to provide users with stronger anonymity services.

title: A Host-Based Multi Module Intrusion Detection Framework for Secure Public Wi-Fi Using Metadata Based Analysis and Real Time Risk Advisory
authors: Dewmini Liyanage; D. Anuradha; Dineth Thv; S. Jayasinghe; K. Abeywardena; D. Pandithage
abstract: Public Wi-Fi networks are widely used for convenient internet access, yet they expose users to major cyber security threats such as rogue access points, DNS manipulation, encrypted malware command and control (C2) communication and unsafe access to sensitive web applications. Traditional intrusion detection systems have failed to provide sufficient protection because they rely heavily on deep packet inspection, a method that is ineffective in modern encrypted environments and raises privacy concerns. This paper introduces a python and machine learning based privacy preserving, multi module IDS framework designed specifically for public Wi-Fi environments which is capable of detecting multiple threat vectors using only flow level metadata. For a solution to this ongoing problem, this system integrates four specialized detection modules: DNS anomaly detection, encrypted botnet and C2 activity detection, rogue access point (Evil Twin) identification, and sensitive web access (banking session) detection. Each module analyzes statistical and behavioral features such as packet size distributions, inter-arrival times, domain entropy, TLS fingerprints, and signal characteristics without inspecting packet payloads. A weighted risk fusion model is introduced to combine detection outputs and generate a unified risk score which is further translated into real time, context aware security advisories for end users. This framework is implemented as a software-based solution that operates at the network monitoring layer enabling real time analysis of encrypted traffic without requiring specialized hardware or modifications to user devices. Experimental evaluation using benchmark datasets and controlled test scenarios demonstrates strong detection performance for wireless layer threats and sensitive-session identification while maintaining low latency and efficient resource utilization, with reduced recall against low-rate encrypted C2 and DNS attacks identified as a documented limitation. A complementary capability analysis against a commercial endpoint detection and response (EDR) agent further shows that the framework provides visibility into wireless layer and contextual risks that endpoint-centric solutions do not cover. The results highlight the effectiveness of combining multiple metadata driven detection techniques into a unified framework, offering a practical and scalable approach for enhancing security in public Wi-Fi networks without compromising user privacy.

title: A Hybrid CNN-BiLSTM-Attention Framework for Multi-Class Web Attack Detection in IoT Environments
authors: Ze-Tong Liu
venue: 2026 International Conference on Vision, Advanced Imaging and Computer Technology (VAICT)
abstract: With the rapid development of Internet of Things (IoT) technologies, an increasing number of devices are connected to the Internet, which significantly expands the attack surface of network systems. Traditional rule-based or signature-based intrusion detection methods have difficulty identifying complex and evolving web attacks. To address this problem, this paper proposes a hybrid deep learning model based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM), and an Attention Mechanism for multi-class web attack detection. The model employs multiscale Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to extract local features from Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) request sequences, bidirectional long short-term memory networks to capture contextual dependencies, and an attention mechanism to emphasize critical features related to attacks. Experiments conducted on a large-scale IoT web attack dataset demonstrate that the proposed model achieves an accuracy of 97.08% and a weighted F1-score of 0.9707, outperforming several traditional machine learning and deep learning baselines. The results indicate that the proposed architecture effectively improves the detection capability for complex web attack patterns in IoT environments.

title: A Hybrid CNN-SelfAttention Model for Anomaly Detection in Encrypted Traffic Metadata
authors: Sabuhee Sabuhee; Pratik Buchke
venue: Technix International Journal for Engineering Research
abstract: This study introduces a deep learning framework integrating convolutional neural networks and self-attention mechanisms for anomaly detection in encrypted network traffic, addressing the limitations of traditional methods reliant on payload inspection. Utilizing the UNSW-NB15 dataset, the approach preprocesses metadata to handle class imbalance, missing values, and categorical features, followed by training a hybrid model combining Conv1D layers for local feature extraction and self-attention for capturing long-range dependencies. The model achieves a test accuracy and F1-score of 0.9927, surpassing classical machine learning models (best F1-score of 0.9284) and a baseline LSTM-self-attention model (best F1-score of 0.7355). Its computational efficiency supports real-time applications, offering a privacy-preserving solution for detecting threats like DDoS attacks and malware. This research advances network security by providing a scalable and robust framework for encrypted traffic analysis.

title: A Hybrid Machine Learning Model for Enhanced Multi-Protocol Malware Detection in Darknet Traffic
authors: Riya; A. Arora; F. Etyang; Ngaira Mandela
venue: International Conference on Computing for Sustainable Global Development
abstract: This study addresses the challenge of detecting multi-protocol malware in darknet traffic by developing a hybrid machine learning model. In an anonymized, encrypted darknet where malware travels over SMTP, HTTP, and FTP protocols, traditional signature-based detection models are inefficient. We used a stacking ensemble algorithm, which combines Random Forest and Neural Networks, tested on the CICDarknet2020 dataset on $\mathbf{k}$-fold cross-validation. Our hybrid model had a higher accuracy of 98.05 % compared to the Random Forest (97.45 %), Neural Networks (96.2 %), SVM (92.85 %), the KNN (93.2 %), and the Gradient Boosting $(96.55 \%)$. The model proved more precise (98.07 %), with a higher recall (98.1 %), although the model has high specificity $(99.93 \%)$. SHAP analysis provided the following metrics as the most significant to classify BwdInitWin Bytes, FWDInitWin Bytes, and idle time. The stacking method minimized false negatives of advanced malware by 68 % in comparison to individual algorithms. The results of this study support the idea that ensemble approaches are effective in balancing detection and generalization ability on multi-protocol malware detection, and serve as a powerful structure to detect emerging threats in darknet setups.
