title: A Hybrid Structural and TF-IDF-Based Machine Learning Framework for Large-Scale Phishing URL Detection
authors: Handayani Linda; Ety Sutanty; Esti Setiyaningsih
abstract: Phishing attacks continue to pose significant cybersecurity risks by exploiting deceptive URLs to obtain sensitive user information, thereby necessitating accurate and scalable automated detection mechanisms.This study proposes a machine learning-based approach for phishing URL classification by integrating structural URL feature extraction with Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques using Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF).The dataset comprises 822,010 labeled URLs, consisting of 52% legitimate and 48% phishing instances, with prior validation to ensure the absence of missing values.Feature engineering was conducted through two complementary strategies: handcrafted structural features-including URL length, domain length, number of digits, special characters, suspicious keywords, HTTPS usage, and number of subdomains and TF-IDF based textual representation using unigram, bigram, and trigram tokenization.The combined feature set was used to train a Random Forest classifier with optimized hyperparameters, and model evaluation was performed using Stratified 5-Fold Cross Validation to preserve class distribution across training and testing subsets.Performance assessment was conducted using confusion matrix, precision, recall, and F1-score to provide a comprehensive evaluation of detection capability.The experimental findings indicate that the integration of structural and textual features significantly improves classification effectiveness, enabling robust and balanced detection of phishing and legitimate URLs, thus demonstrating the practical applicability of the proposed method for large-scale real-world deployment.

title: A Lightweight Deep Learning Framework for Encrypted Traffic Classification via Visual Flow Representation
authors: Zengyu Cai; Banghao Liang; Jianwei Zhang; Liang Zhu; Ying Hu
venue: Concurrency and Computation Practice and Experience
abstract: ABSTRACT With the increasing complexity of cybersecurity threats, encrypted network traffic is becoming more and more widely used in all kinds of malicious communications. Traditional feature engineering‐based machine learning methods encounter accuracy and scalability issues when identifying such traffic, while existing deep learning methods achieve high accuracy but have large parameter counts and poor portability. Based on this, this paper for the first time migrates and applies the Lightweight Deep Learning Framework for Encrypted Traffic Classification via Visual Flow Representation to the MobileViT architecture. This paper presents the first application of the lightweight deep learning model MobileViT architecture to the task of classifying encrypted network traffic. We designed structural adaptations tailored for time‐series network data and constructed an enhanced variant, MiTNet, specifically suited for this task, which integrates a convolutional neural network and a visual Transformer architecture to achieve high‐accuracy classification of encrypted network traffic. The model employs 1D depth‐separable convolution to construct lightweight inverted residual blocks, which extract local temporal features, and combines this with the MobileViT module to establish global dependencies, thereby improving the recognition of different traffic types. The experiments are evaluated on four typical network traffic classification datasets, and the model achieves more than 98% accuracy and F1 scores on all four datasets while maintaining a very low number of parameters, balancing accuracy and inference efficiency, demonstrating the feasibility and superiority of the lightweight model for encrypted traffic recognition.

title: A Lightweight Frequency-Domain Defense Framework for Adversarially Robust Wearable ECG Classification
authors: Kehang Lai
venue: Fundamental Scientific Reports in Multidisciplinary Areas
abstract: With the development of different kinds of wearable devices, more and more people are using these systems monitoring their body signals. In addition, deep neural networks show strong performance when it comes to single-lead ECG rhythm classification. However, those machine learning classifiers can be easily affected by small deliberately designed adversarial perturbations to original input data. Hence, this essay proposes a lightweight frequency-domain defense framework for protecting a single-lead ECG classifier against adversarial perturbations using the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database. The experiment in this essay uses both patient-level train/test separation and continuous multi-beat ECG windows, so the evaluation is closer to a real-world clinical setting where new patients are unseen during training. This framework uses FGSM and PGD to attack an unprotected baseline model trained by time-series based 1D CNN (one-dimensional convolutional neural network) and a proposed frequency-domain trained 1D CNN defense model. In particular, the baseline receives normalized fixed length temporal windows, while the defense receives normalized FFT (Fast Fourier Transform) transformed frequency sequences. Also, both models are evaluated with the introduced adversarial attacks. Thus, across five random patient-level splits and 11 perturbation strengths, the result shows that the defense model achieved higher mean attacked macro F1 for all three attack families: 0.676 versus 0.419 for FGSM, 0.483 versus 0.248 for PGD, and 0.482 versus 0.248 for the combined attack. All in all, the main contribution in this essay is a lightweight framework that changes the classifier input from a temporal window to FFT-magnitude features and trains this frequency-domain model with clean, FGSM, and short-PGD samples. The code can be accessed at GitHub (https://github.com/ArcaneEmerald/ecg-defense-framework).

title: A Lightweight-Based Transformer Model for Detecting Phishing E-Mails
authors: Asmaa Elsaid; Asmaa Elkhouly; Shimaa Osman
abstract: In the contemporary digital security landscape, phishing email attacks stand out as exceptionally cunning and perilous cyber threats. These attacks employ sophisticated impersonation methodologies to target particular individuals or entities. Diverging from conventional phishing strategies, these advanced attacks are precisely targeted and meticulously crafted, thereby evading the effectiveness of standard detection mechanisms that rely on generalized patterns and recurring phrases, which often fail to recognize the unique attributes of these tailored threats, such as their specific language, context, and the personal information they exploit to deceive victims. This paper presents a proposed approach that uses the TinyBERT model, an artificial intelligence model, with fused open-source intelligence (OSINT) features, including domain age, SSL certificate validity, sender reputation, and characteristics of embedded links, to build more reliable and adaptive phishing detection systems. The proposed approach is designed for use in resource-limited environments, such as small and medium enterprises, that require effective solutions without a significant demand for computing power. The integration of the dataset and OSINT improves the model's ability to understand the message's true context, allowing it to analyze not only the text but also descriptive signals about the sender's technical structure and content. Four models (TinyBert, MobileBERT, and BERTBased) were trained on both the original text and the OSINT-fused dataset. Ten experiments are applied, and the experimental results indicate that the proposed approach outperforms state-of-the-art machine learning algorithms. Index Terms-Phishing email detection, Transformer models, TinyBERT, MobileBERT, BERT-Base, OSINT features, and text classification.

title: A Machine Learning Framework for Robust Java API Security: Enhancing Vulnerability Detection and Mitigation
authors: Gaurav Gupta
venue: Journal of Research in Science and Engineering
abstract: Securing Java APIs is vital in today's interconnected world. APIs are gateways for data exchange. They face constant threats, such as unauthorized access and malicious payloads. With the rise of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML), traditional security measures like HTTPS, OAuth 2.0, and JSON Web Tokens (JWT) can now integrate advanced threat detection. AI and ML offer real - time anomaly detection, token validation, and communication layer protection. They help identify threats earlier, reducing the risks of data breaches. This article looks at the role of AI and ML in enhancing Java API security. It discusses their use in detecting threats, ensuring token integrity, and maintaining secure communication. These technologies strengthen API defense mechanisms, enabling safer and more reliable digital ecosystems.

title: A Machine Learning-Based Anomaly Detection in Digital Power Grid Network Traffic
authors: Peng Xiao
abstract: With the in-depth construction of digital power grids, their cyber-physical systems face severe cybersecurity challenges. Malicious encrypted traffic, using HTTPS and SSL/TLS, threatens grid stability, making traditional detection ineffective. This paper focuses on such traffic from mainstream hacking tools, combines network traffic analysis with machine learning, extracts protocol layer features, and constructs decision tree, random forest, and LSTM models. Experiments show their accuracy rates reach 99.85%, 99.93%, and 99.64% respectively, enabling intelligent and accurate detection, providing technical support for grid security.

title: A Machine Learning-Based Approach for Detecting DNS Tunneling and Data Exfiltration in Network Traffic
authors: Ajay; Deepika Kumawat; Atharv Sharma; Adarsh Gokhe; Nikhil Agalcha; Rinku Patil
venue: International Journal of Computer Information Systems and Industrial Management Applications
abstract: The Domain Name System (DNS) is a foundational protocol of the Internet, and its near-universal permission through firewalls makes it an attractive covert channel for attackers seeking to tunnel data or exfiltrate sensitive information. DNS tunneling techniques encode arbitrary data inside DNS queries and responses, allowing adversaries to bypass conventional perimeter defenses that focus on HTTP, HTTPS, and other well-monitored protocols. Signature-based intrusion detection systems struggle to keep pace with the diversity of tunneling tools and obfuscation strategies, motivating the application of machine learning (ML) to this problem. This paper presents a comprehensive machine learning-based framework for detecting DNS tunneling and data exfiltration activity in network traffic. We extract a rich set of statistical, lexical, and temporal features from DNS query streams and evaluate nine classification approaches, including Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, k-Nearest Neighbors, Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machine, Random Forest, XGBoost, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, and a proposed hybrid Convolutional Neural Network-Random Forest (CNN-RF) ensemble. Experiments conducted on a labeled dataset of benign and tunneled DNS traffic show that the proposed hybrid model achieves 98.4% accuracy, 98.1% precision, 98.7% recall, and an F1-score of 98.4%, outperforming all baseline classifiers and prior published approaches. The results demonstrate that combining automatically learned representations with engineered statistical features substantially improves detection of low-and-slow exfiltration and previously unseen tunneling tools.

title: A method for comprehensively assessing the effectiveness of using content destruction and reconstruction technology in network infrastructure
authors: А.В. Яцев; І. М. Журавель
abstract: The article explores the possibilities of using Content Disarm and Reconstruction (CDR) technology to increasethe effectiveness of network resource protection during processing and transfer of files of various formats. The relevanceof the study is due to the rapid increase in the dangers associated with the growth of the number of hidden threatsimplemented through legitimate file structures and capable of bypassing traditional means of detecting malicious content,which causes a high level of complexity in their prevention or neutralization. The main attention is focused on developinga method for comprehensive experimental assessment of the effectiveness of using CDR solutions as a means ofpreventive countermeasures against threats that arise during the exchange of files with potentially malicious content. Thework considers the basics of the content security problem and the idea of its cleaning as one of the ways to solve it, aswell as the principle of operation of the content disarm and reconstruction technology, which consists in removing activeand potentially dangerous elements of the file with the subsequent formation of its safe copy based on the standardstructure of the corresponding file format that was processed. The features of CDR application to various types of files,in particular documents, archives, images and multimedia content, are analyzed, and its advantages compared to classicalsignature and behavioral protection tools, such as antiviruses and sandbox detection methods, are also identified. Anexperimental methodology for mass testing CDR solutions on large volumes of files is proposed with further analysis ofthe results and formation of a system of quantitative performance indicators that take into account the level ofneutralization of hidden threats, reconstruction correctness, processing performance and impact on network andcomputing resources. As a result, directions for further research are identified, in particular, clarification of optimalscenarios for the use of content neutralization and reconstruction technology, formalization of efficiency criteria anddevelopment of methods for optimizing performance while maintaining high quality of file reconstruction.Keywords: cybersecurity; information protection; network security; content disarm. title: A METHOD FOR FORMING A SOCIAL ENGINEER PROFILE BASED ON A DETECTED PHISHING ATTACK ON AN INFORMATION SYSTEM
authors: А. О. Корченко; М. Г. Аскеров; Кирило ДАВИДЕНКО; А.А. Герасименко; Ю.С. Журов
abstract: Phishing attacks remain one of the most widespread cyber threat vectors, as they combine technical mechanismsfor compromising information systems with social engineering techniques. At the same time, existing phishing detectionapproaches are primarily focused on analyzing the technical parameters of an attack and do not provide a formalizedtransition from detection results to identifying the characteristics of the attacker, which complicates cyberattackattribution, cyber threat intelligence, and information security incident response. The aim of this study is to develop amethod for constructing a social engineer profile based on the analysis of a detected phishing attack on an informationsystem. The proposed method is based on extending a generalized tuple by integrating a set of attacker profile featuresformed according to the set-theoretic classification model of modern social engineering attack implementation approachesand the parameters of the detected phishing attack. The method consists of four main stages: constructing a formalizedrepresentation of the phishing attack, determining the characteristics of the social engineer profile, constructing anintegrated social engineer profile, and visualizing the resulting profile. Unlike existing approaches, the proposed methodprovides a formalized transition from the parameters of a detected phishing attack to the construction of an integratedprofile of its perpetrator. The proposed method was validated using a representative phishing attack, resulting in theconstruction of a social engineer profile, identification of its key characteristics, and generation of a diagram that providesa graphical representation of the resulting profile. The obtained results can be used to support cyberattack attribution,cyber threat intelligence, information security incident response, and the development of countermeasures against socialengineering attacks.Keywords: phishing, social engineer profile, attacker profile, social engineering, cyber threat intelligence,information security. title: A Multi-Modal AI Framework for Intrusion Detection in Healthcare IoT
authors: Hani Al‐Balasmeh; Fayzeh Abdulkareem Jaber; Saeed  Serwan Abdulsattar
venue: International Journal of Basic and Applied Sciences
abstract: The rapid adoption of Healthcare Internet of Things (HIoT) technologies has increased the exposure of safety-critical medical infrastructures ‎to sophisticated cyberattacks, while simultaneously imposing strict constraints on availability, privacy, and false alarm tolerance. Traditional ‎network-centric intrusion detection systems (IDSs) struggle to reliably detect stealthy, low-rate attacks in healthcare environments, where ‎encrypted traffic and predictable clinical communication patterns limit observability. This paper proposes a lightweight multi-modal intrusion ‎detection framework for HIoT networks that jointly analyzes network flow metadata and device telemetry using structured feature fusion ‎and ensemble meta-learning. By integrating communication behavior with device-level operational regularity, the framework provides a ‎more comprehensive representation of system activity without relying on payload inspection. An extensive evaluation was conducted using ‎heterogeneous IoT and botnet datasets, including TON_IoT, IoT-23, and MedBIoT, under realistic conditions of class imbalance. Experi-‎mental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves 97.1% detection accuracy and 96.5% F1-score, outperforming state-of-‎the-art network-only IDS baselines. Most notably, the framework reduces the false positive rate to 2.4%, representing a relative reduction ‎of over 38% compared to strong deep learning baselines. Attack-wise analysis shows the most significant performance gains for stealthy ‎and low-rate attack classes, where network-centric IDSs exhibit substantial degradation. Ablation studies confirm that device telemetry im-‎proves recall for stealthy threats, while ensemble meta-learning stabilizes predictions and suppresses false alarms. Latency and scalability ‎measurements further indicate that the framework remains suitable for real-time deployment at healthcare gateway nodes. Overall, the results ‎provide strong empirical evidence that multi-modal intrusion detection materially improves detection reliability, clinical safety, and robust-‎ness in healthcare IoT environments, addressing key limitations of existing single-modality IDS approaches.

title: A multi-session EEG and upper extremity assessment dataset during stroke rehabilitation with the ReHand-BCI
authors: Jessica Cantillo-Negrete; Martín Emiliano Rodríguez-García; Ruben I. Carino-Escobar; Paul Carrillo-Mora; Ana G. Ramirez-Nava; Claudia Hernández-Arenas et al.
abstract: DATASET INFORMATIONAn electroencephalography (EEG) dataset collected from 19 stroke patients that underwent up to 30 therapy sessions during the ReHand-BCI clinical trial (registration: NCT04724824, https://doi.org/10.3389/fnins.2025.1579988), using a Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) system developed for upper extremity (UE) motor rehabilitation, is presented. The dataset also includes the participants’ demographic and clinical information, trial-related annotations consisting of artifact presence and ReHand-BCI feedback information, and clinical assessments scores for UE motor function evaluation, specifically the FMA-UE and the ARAT scores.This data is intended to support diverse research applications, including the characterization of stroke-related brain dynamics, the development of EEG-based biomarkers of UE motor recovery, the evaluation of EEG signal-processing methods, the training and testing of machine learning models, and the development of BCI or neurofeedback systems.ParticipantsTen participants were allocated to the experimental group, where the BCI was controlled by the participants’ motor intention (MI) of their paralyzed hand by performing the intent of a grasping task to activate a robotic hand orthosis, providing passive finger flexion and extension. The control group was comprised by 9 participants who received a sham-BCI intervention, where the robotic orthosis activated randomly without depending on the user’s MI. In each therapy session, participants performed up to 80 MI-based trials, while raw EEG was acquired from 16 electrodes located over the motor cortex of both brain hemispheres.ReHand-BCI systemThe ReHand-BCI system consisted of a computer monitor that provided instructions, in the form of visual and auditory cues, to the patients and three stages: acquisition, processing, and feedback. The acquisition stage was comprised by a g.USBamp amplifier (g.tec medical engineering GmbH, Austria), a g.GAMMAbox preamplifier (g.tec), and 16 g.LadyBird active electrodes (g.tec). EEG data was acquired at 256 Hz with a 24-bit A/D resolution. The electrodes were located at the F3, FC3, C5, C3, C1, CP3, P3, FCz, Cz, F4, FC4, C6, C4, C2, CP4, and P4 positions using an EEG cap marked with the 10-10 system of a size that fitted the participants’ head and centred around the Cz position. A monopolar recording was performed with an active ground electrode placed on the AFz position and a passive reference electrode placed on the right earlobe. The processing stage, implemented in a Precision 5820 workstation (Dell Inc., Texas, USA) and programmed in a MATLAB R2017a (MathWorks Inc., Massachusetts, USA) Graphical User Interface, consisted in two modes, an offline calibration mode and an online therapy mode. For calibration, previously recorded EEG data from the preceding therapy session was used to determine subject-specific parameters. These features were selected via Particle Swarm Optimization to determine relevant Common Spatial Patterns parameters extracted from the 8–12, 12–16, 16–20, 20–24, 24–28, and 28–32 Hz frequency bands of the prerecorded EEG data, following the Filter Bank Common Spatial Patterns framework. Lastly, the selected features were used to train a Linear Discriminant Analysis for task classification purposes.In the therapy mode, 1 s windows of EEG data acquired online were classified as either hand MI or as rest using the selected subject-specific parameters obtained in the calibration mode. The feedback stage consisted in a robotic hand orthosis that provided to the participant's paralyzed hand passive finger flexion and extension. The robotic orthosis was activated via a Bluetooth command sent by the processing stage if the system detected the user’s hand MI for the EG, or randomly if the participant was allotted to the CG. Further technical details of the ReHand-BCI system can be found in previous studies (https://doi.org/10.1155/2018/1624637, https://doi.org/10.3389/fnbot.2023.1015464).Therapy sessionsAll participants received up to 30 1-hour therapy sessions, provided daily from Monday to Friday for a total of 6 weeks. Participants performed 4 runs of 20 trials each in every therapy session.Outcome measuresPrimary outcome measures were two clinical assessments: the FMA-UE, which evaluates UE sensorimotor function (https://doi.org/10.1177/1545968313491000), and the ARAT, which measures UE functional performance (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.apmr.2006.09.003). A clinical assessment session was performed at baseline (T0), after the 15th therapy session (T1), and after the intervention (T2), for a total of three evaluations. For every participant, the same expert clinician performed all 3 assessments sessions, who remained blinded to group allocation throughout the intervention period.DATASET DESCRIPTIONThis dataset is fully described in the article "A multi-session EEG and upper extremity assessment dataset during stroke rehabilitation with the ReHand-BCI".The dataset is comprised by an .xlsx file named “Participants_Information.xlsx” and by ZIP files named after the participants’ ID. The coded demographic and clinical information of the participants is provided on the “Information” sheet of the .xlsx file, whereas the corresponding codes can be found on the “Coding” sheet. Each ZIP file contains two folder levels and, inside the second-level folder, Comma-Separated Values (CSV) format files. For every participant, EEG data acquired during each therapy session and the FMA-UE and ARAT scores obtained from the three clinical assessments were included in the dataset. At the first folder level after decompressing the ZIP files, folders state the participants’ ID, with the second level folders named either as the therapy session number (S1, S2, …, or S30) or as the clinical assessment session number (T0, T1, or T2).Electroencephalography dataIn the therapy session folders, the acquired EEG data can be found in CSV format files, divided by completed runs. The filename of the CSV EEG data is comprised by the participant’s ID, the therapy session number, and the run number. For instance, for participant P4, therapy session S15, and run 3 (R3), the filename is “P4_S15_R3.csv”. In the clinical assessment session folders, two CSV files can be found, each one containing the clinical score of either the FMA-UE or the ARAT assessment of the corresponding session. The names of these files are comprised by the participant’s ID, the assessment session number, and the clinical evaluation abbreviation. For example, for participant P12, clinical assessment session T2, and for the FMA-UE score (FMAUE), the filename is “P12_T2_FMAUE.csv”.If a participant did not attend a therapy session, the corresponding folder is absent from the database. Additionally, if a participant performed, due to time constraints, only 3 runs in a therapy session, three EEG CSV files are found in the corresponding folder. Participant P2 performed eight 10-trial runs, instead of the standard four 20-trial runs, from therapy session S12 to S30 due to patient’s fatigue.The therapy session CSV files comprise 19 rows. The first row contains labels that denote the trial period to which every sample (column) belongs to in the continuous EEG recording for each run. The rest period (0 to 4 s of the trial’s time structure) was denoted as “Rs”, the MI period (4 to 9 s) was designated as “MI”, the relaxation period (9 to 14 s) was referred to as “Rl”, and the random interval period was denoted as “Rn”. Thus, for example, a sample (column) that belongs to the 17th trial (T17), in the relaxation period (Rl), of a participant whose affected hand was the right (R) hand, has the label “T17_Rl_R” in the first row of that particular column. Row 2 contains coded characters to indicate if the trials were removed (r) or kept (k) to perform the cortical activity longitudinal analysis presented in the Technical Validation section. These characters only appear in the first column of each trial, with the remaining columns left blank. Row 3 indicates the output value of the ReHand-BCI’s processing stage in the rest and the MI periods. A value of 1 indicates that the system’s Linear Discriminant Analysis classified the previous 1 s EEG window as “MI”, whereas a value of 0 reflects a “rest” classification. These values are found in the column after each 1 s EEG window of the rest (at 1, 2, 3, and 4 s) and the MI (at 5, 6, 7, and 8 s) periods. The remaining columns in the row are blank. Rows 4 to 19 contain the acquired raw EEG electrode signals in the following order, which corresponds to their original electrode configuration: F3, FC3, C5, C3, C1, CP3, P3, FCz, Cz, F4, FC4, C6, C4, C2, CP4, and P4. Each column in these rows represents a sample value acquired from each EEG electrode expressed in µV and without filtering, thus being raw data. The number of columns differ in the CSV files due to the random duration of each trial.Clinical assessments dataEach clinical assessment session CSV file contains two rows and one column. The first row shows a label that is comprised by the session number and the clinical scale abbreviation. For example, the label of the T1 ARAT score is “T1_ARAT”. The second row shows the obtained score in the clinical assessment.

title: A Multi-Stage AI-Driven Recognition and Dynamic Defense Framework for DDoS Attacks
authors: Jian-Wen Huang
venue: 2026 6th International Conference on Computer Science and Blockchain (CCSB)
abstract: Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks continue to pose one of the most persistent threats to network availability. In recent years, attackers have evolved from simple volumetric floods to sophisticated multi-vector campaigns, and the adversarial adoption of artificial intelligence has further accelerated the evolution of attack techniques, rendering traditional static threshold and signature-based detection systems increasingly inadequate. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an artificial intelligence-based multi-stage DDoS recognition and dynamic defense framework. The framework comprises three sequentially integrated stages: (1) a lightweight anomaly pre-screening module based on multi-feature entropy analysis that triggers initial alerts with minimal computational overhead ; (2) a hybrid deep learning detection engine combining Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for spatial feature extraction and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) networks for temporal dependency modeling, optimized via recursive feature elimination for dimensionality reduction ; and (3) a dynamic mitigation module employing Deep Reinforcement Learning with Double Deep Q-Networks (DDQN) to adaptively adjust rate-limiting, traffic redirection, and filtering strategies in real time based on current network state. Extensive experiments on CIC-IDS-2017 and CICDDoS2019 benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves detection accuracy exceeding 99.2% with an average detection latency of 1.07 seconds (including a 1-second traffic aggregation window), while maintaining a false positive rate below 0.5%. Under real-world attack simulations, the system sustains over 95% detection accuracy and effectively mitigates diverse attack vectors including HTTP floods, SYN floods, and botnet-driven volumetric attacks. The results confirm that the proposed multi-stage AI framework offers a practical, deployable solution for real-time DDoS defense with strong generalization capabilities across heterogeneous network environments.

title: A Novel Contrastive Loss for Zero-Day Network Intrusion Detection
authors: Jack Wilkie; Hanan Hindy; Craig Michie; Christos Tachtatzis; James M. Irvine; Robert C. Atkinson
venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
abstract: Machine learning has achieved state-of-the-art results in network intrusion detection; however, its performance significantly degrades when confronted by a new attack class— a zero-day attack. In simple terms, classical machine learning-based approaches are adept at identifying attack classes on which they have been previously trained, but struggle with those not included in their training data. One approach to addressing this shortcoming is to utilise anomaly detectors which train exclusively on benign data with the goal of generalising to all attack classes— both known and zero-day. However, this comes at the expense of a prohibitively high false positive rate. This work proposes a novel contrastive loss function which is able to maintain the advantages of other contrastive learning-based approaches (robustness to imbalanced data) but can also generalise to zero-day attacks. Unlike anomaly detectors, this model learns the distributions of benign traffic using both benign and known malign samples, i.e. other well-known attack classes (not including the zero-day class), and consequently, achieves significant performance improvements. The proposed approach is experimentally verified on the Lycos2017 dataset where it achieves an AUROC improvement of.000065 and.060883 over previous models in known and zero-day attack detection, respectively. Finally, the proposed method is extended to open-set recognition achieving OpenAUC improvements of.170883 over existing approaches.The implementation and experiments are open-sourced and available at: https://github.com/jackwilkie/CLOSR

title: A Novel Self-Supervised Learning Approach for Anomaly Detection in Adversarial Network Traffic
authors: Anjali Awasthi; Sumita Mishra; Shriram Kris Vasudevan; Jyoti Grover
venue: International Conference on Computing, Sciences and Communications (ICCSC)
abstract: The increasing complexity and frequency of cyber attacks have created a dire need for a more resilient and adaptive network Intrusion Detection System(NIDS). Traditional anomaly detection systems face a serious challenge from the rise of sophisticated cyberattacks, especially hostile manipulations of network traffic. To avoid signature-based and even some anomaly-based detectors, these attacks are made to look like legitimate traffic. The lack of labeled attack data is a significant obstacle to creating strong defenses. In order to overcome this data scarcity of labeled attack data, this paper suggests a novel approach using selfsupervised learning (SSL) framework for anomaly detection in networks which makes use of enormous volumes of unlabeled normal traffic. Our method pre-trains a multi-modal encoder by combining contrastive learning with a set of carefully crafted pretext tasks, including temporal context prediction, conceptual graph structure reconstruction, and a special pseudo-adversarial perturbation prediction/reconstruction task. By explicitly teaching the model to recognize minute, self-generated departures from typical patterns, this pseudo-adversarial task increases the model's sensitivity to actual adversarial manipulations. Robust latent representations are subsequently extracted by the pretrained encoder and fed into a one-class classifier for anomaly detection. Using the difficult CIC-IDS2018 dataset, we compare our SSL approach to a conventional unsupervised Isolation Forest (as a baseline) and a supervised Random Forest classifier (as an upper bound). Our self-supervised approach shows promising results for a reliable as well as a scalable solution for real-world cyber security, as preliminary results show that it significantly outperforms traditional unsupervised methods in detecting both generic anomalies and stealthy adversarial traffic.

title: A PIPELINE FOR CREATING OBFUSCATED BINARY SAMPLES TO TRAIN AI-POWERED DETECTION MODELS
authors: Luka Wilmink
abstract: The analysis of binary files is a critical component of antivirus software and is one of the most important tools for incident response teams across the industry. In the field, malware is often obfuscated, a practice in which the compilation process is transformed with different techniques to hinder decompilation and reverse engineering. Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning techniques can assist, but models need to be trained on well constructed datasets first. This paper outlines a pipeline for creating such a dataset and builds a proof-of-concept machine learning classification model. All associated data and code are supplied in the project GitHub repository at https://github.com/Papaya-Messiah/GOOBER.

title: A Protocol-Language Model for Network Intrusion (Without Deep Packet Inspection)
authors: Vivek Kumar Sharma
abstract: Modern network intrusion detection systems (NIDS) are caught in a structural contradiction: the protocols carrying the highest threat intelligence are precisely those encrypted under TLS 1.3 and QUIC, where payload inspection yields nothing. We ask a simpler question -- what if the attack signature is not in the bytes, but in the rhythm? -- and answer it by treating network flows as a language whose grammar is written entirely in L3/L4 packet metadata: length, inter-arrival time, TTL, TCP flags, and hashed port numbers. We present PLM-NIDS, which proves three claims in sequence. (1) The grammar exists and is learnable: a RWKV-4 state-space model trained on 344,232 unlabelled Monday flows achieves a causal LM validation loss of 0.204, demonstrating that benign traffic has predictable, statistically consistent structure. (2) Attacks violate this grammar: the per-flow perplexity score cleanly separates benign from attack flows with PR-AUC = 0.93 using zero attack labels at training time. (3) This separation is architecturally nontrivial: an LSTM trained on identical token sequences degenerates to a majority-class predictor (ROC-AUC approximately 0.50, F1 = 0.91 by always predicting "attack"), proving that RWKV's causal pre-training provides an inductive bias unavailable to direct classifiers. Supervised fine-tuning further raises PR-AUC to 0.94 and ROC-AUC to 0.75, with a precision of 97.7% at the calibrated operating threshold. The RWKV backbone's O(T) recurrent inference enables per-packet streaming without flow buffering, making PLM-NIDS operationally viable at line rate. Because it reads only IP/TCP/UDP headers, it is inherently encryption-agnostic: TLS 1.3, QUIC, and future encrypted protocols are handled transparently.

title: A Python Program for Automatic Detection of SQL Injection Attacks in Web Applications
authors: Mehmonaliyev Yahyobek; Umarov Abdulmuxtor
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: SQL Injection (SQLi) remains a significant threat to modern web application security. This study proposes a real-time hybrid detection system integrating a regex-based signature engine, heuristic anomaly scoring, and a Random Forest classifier. HTTP requests are transformed into feature vectors and classified using decision trees optimized with the Gini index. Experimental results demonstrate 99% accuracy and a 0.8% false positive rate. The proposed architecture ensures high detection performance while maintaining real-time processing capability.

title: A Quantum-Inspired Intrusion Detection System for Serverless Computing using QMV4ECX framework
authors: Mastanaih Naidu Yasam; Y. Narasimha Rao; N Ramakrishnaiah
abstract: The serverless platform is designed to make it easier to deploy, scale, and manage cloud applications. Unfortunately, it is challenging to directly transfer typical security measures to serverless computing due to its distributed nature. The current serverless solutions mostly use runtime metrics collection, encrypted traffic offloading detection, or post-analysis of modified operating system audit logs to find potential threats. Nevertheless, these techniques frequently fall short of fully identifying cross-functional communication problems. This restriction makes it more difficult to maintain low connection latency and limits real-time log surveillance and verification abilities in dispersed contexts. Therefore, this paper presents an effective deep learning based framework called quantum-inspired MobileNetV4 with Enhanced ConvMiXer (QMV4ECX) for intrusion detection in a serverless computing environment. In this framework, we use Quantum-inspired MobileNetV4 (QMV4) as the feature extractor to gather key characteristics from the network data. The Enhanced ConvMiXer method is then used as the classifier to identify and classify threats. Furthermore, the Wombat Optimization Algorithm (WOA) is utilized to tune the hyperparameters of the classifier. Performance analysis has been conducted using the DoW, MDCD-AINA, and synthetic datasets, and the experimental results show that QMV4ECX can accurately detect a wide range of attacks, enabling thorough function execution tracking and evaluation while drastically reducing performance overhead.

title: A Review of Hybrid Deep Learning Architectures for Real-Time Network Traffic Anomaly Detection: From Signature-Based Systems to Cross-Stream Attention CNN-BiLSTM Frameworks
authors: Rohan Singh; Jitender Kumar
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: The proliferation of encrypted network traffic and the accelerating sophistication of cyber-attack methodologies have rendered signature-based intrusion detection fundamentally inadequate for contemporary Security Operations Centre (SOC) and Network Operations Centre (NOC) environments, a problem underscored by a global cyberattack cost exceeding eight trillion United States dollars in 2023. This paper reviews the methodological evolution of network traffic anomaly detection, tracing the progression from signature-matching platforms through statistical and behavioural baselining to deep learning architectures spanning convolutional neural networks, recurrent and attention-augmented sequence models, graph neural networks, and Transformer-based classifiers. Particular attention is given to the limitations of single-modality architectures, which capture either the spatial packet-level structure or the temporal session-level dynamics of network traffic but not both simultaneously, and to the comparative strengths and weaknesses of early, late, and attention-based multi-stream fusion paradigms. The review further examines loss-level strategies for the severe class imbalance characteristic of intrusion-detection benchmarks, and surveys the explainability mechanisms required for analyst trust and MITRE ATT&CK alignment in production SOC deployment. Based on the gaps identified, the paper discusses an emerging direction—lightweight cross-stream attention CNN-BiLSTM frameworks exemplified by TrafficGuardNet—and outlines future research priorities, including model compression for ultra-high-throughput deployment, continual learning under concept drift, and feature-engineering adaptations for TLS 1.3-encrypted environments.

title: A Review of Machine Learning Driven Automated Ethical Hacking: Proactive Defense and Vulnerability Mitigation in Wi-Fi and LAN Networks
authors: Tharindu Yehan Wanniya Bandara; Dharani Abeysinghe
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: The increasing reliance on Wi-Fi networks has raised significant concerns regarding network security, with vulnerabilities such as de-authentication, man-in-the-middle (MITM), and denial-of-service (DoS) attacks persisting despite advancements in security protocols such as WPA2. Existing tools, including Aircrack-ng and Wireshark, require considerable technical expertise and primarily focus on vulnerability identification without providing automated feedback or proactive defense mechanisms, limiting their accessibility to non-technical users. This study addresses these limitations by integrating machine learning (ML) algorithms, including anomaly detection and classification models, into penetration testing processes. Machine learning enables automated vulnerability assessments, real-time threat detection, and the generation of actionable security recommendations. By analyzing network traffic patterns and identifying irregularities, these algorithms can help predict potential threats and proactively mitigate security risks. Survey findings indicate a strong user preference for automated security tools that provide intuitive guidance and proactive features, such as automatic attacker blocking. Based on these findings, the proposed ML-driven ethical hacking tool aims to simplify network security management for both technical and non-technical users. The tool leverages machine learning not only to identify vulnerabilities but also to recommend dynamic remediation strategies, bridging the gap between technical complexity and usability. The findings of this review highlight the transformative potential of machine learning in modern network security through process automation, improved accessibility, and enhanced proactive defenses for Wi-Fi and LAN networks. By addressing key limitations in existing penetration testing approaches, this research contributes to the development of innovative, efficient, and user-friendly solutions for mitigating network vulnerabilities in an increasingly interconnected world. An abstract of this work was published in the 5th Student Symposium, Faculty of Computing, General Sir John Kotelawala Defence University, held on 6 February 2025: abstract ID 87, printed page 35; e-book ISBN 978-624-6427-44-3. Related abstract: https://ir.kdu.ac.lk/handle/345/8286 This deposit contains the full author manuscript, not the one-page published symposium abstract. It is described here as a preprint; this deposit does not establish peer-reviewed publication of the full manuscript.

title: A Robust Out-of-Distribution Detection Framework via Synergistic Smoothing
authors: Marian Stoica; A. Hekal; Alessio Lomuscio
venue: 2026 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition- FINDINGS Track (CVPRF)
abstract: Reliable out-of-distribution (OOD) detection is a critical requirement for the safe deployment of machine learning systems. Despite recent progress, state-of-the-art OOD detectors are highly susceptible to adversarial attacks, which undermines their trustworthiness in automated systems. To address this vulnerability, we apply median smoothing to baseline OOD detection scores, balancing clean and adversarial accuracies. Our key insight is that the noisy samples generated for median smoothing can be repurposed to quantify the local instability of the base score. We observe that OOD samples exhibit higher instability under perturbation. Based on this, we propose ROSS, a novel and robust post-hoc OOD detector that leverages the instability of baseline scores to further distinguish between in-distribution (ID) and OOD samples. ROSS achieves symmetric robustness, performing strongly against both score-minimising and score-maximising attacks, unlike prior work. This symmetric defence leads to state-ofthe-art robustness, outperforming prior methods by up to 40 AUROC points. We demonstrate ROSS's effectiveness on extensive experiments across CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet. Code is available at: https://github.com/Abdu-Hekal/ROSS.

title: A Secure And Scalable Architecture For Fingerprint Databases In Iot Ecosystems: Integration Of Zero Trust, Blockchain Logging, And Encrypted Microservices
authors: Dr. Akshara Dave Aafrin Julaya
venue: Journal of Informatics Education and Research
abstract: As IoT-based authentication systems rapidly advance, fingerprint biometrics have become crucial for identity verification. However, the incorporation of fingerprint databases within IoT environments poses considerable challenges regarding security, storage, and real-time data communication, particularly in resource-limited settings. Contemporary applications, ranging from smart homes to national identification systems, require highly secure and low-latency handling of fingerprint information. To address current security needs, fingerprint database architectures have progressed into multi-layered systems that incorporate various sophisticated mechanisms. Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA) mandates stringent, ongoing authentication alongside detailed role-based access control. End-to-End Encryption (E2EE) secures data during transmission and when stored using standards such as AES-256, RSA-4096, and TLS 1.3 with mutual authentication. Tokenization and cancelable biometrics alter fingerprint data to hinder reverse engineering and minimize the risk of data breaches. Systems are increasingly implemented as microservices within containerized platforms like Docker or Kubernetes, facilitating improved scalability, isolation, and fault tolerance. Immutable blockchain logging, commonly utilizing platforms like Hyperledger Fabric, guarantees unalterable records of database access and changes to fingerprint templates. Furthermore, AI-driven intrusion detection systems (IDS) monitor access patterns in real-time to identify spoofing attempts and insider threats. Together, these advancements provide a secure, scalable, and compliant foundation for fingerprint databases in contemporary IoT ecosystems.

title: A Serverless Client-Side Privacy Index for Sensitive Data Processing
authors: José Gameiro; J. L. Oliveira; João Rafael Almeida
venue: International Conference on Data Technologies and Applications
abstract: : The widespread adoption of data-driven systems has intensified concerns regarding the protection of sensitive information and the assessment of privacy risks. Although numerous privacy-preserving techniques and models have been proposed, quantifying and interpreting the level of privacy achieved remains challenging, particularly for non-expert users. This paper introduces the Privacy Index, a unified metric designed to aggregate multiple privacy-related factors into a single, interpretable score. The proposed approach integrates the validation of established privacy models, detection of anonymization techniques, and estimation of re-identification risk under different attacker assumptions. To support practical usage, we develop a serverless, client-side web application that automatically processes structured datasets by classifying attributes and computing the Privacy Index without transmitting data externally. Experimental evaluation demonstrates that the attribute classification component achieves average confidence levels above 88% across multiple datasets, correctly identifying all direct identifiers with high reliability. The system successfully validates privacy models such as k -anonymity and l -diversity and effectively distinguishes between poorly and well-anonymized datasets. The tool is open-source, its code is available at https://github.com/ieeta-mith/DataPrivScore and a demo is available through https://ieeta-mith.github.io/DataPrivScore/.

title: A Stacking Enriched Explainable Machine Learning Approach for Multiclass DoS Attack and Network Intrusion Prediction
authors: Maimuna Tabassum; Umme Saima Tonny; Sabila Anzum; Kahakashan Ashraf; Payel Sen; Mahfuzulhoq Chowdhury
venue: International Conference on Circuit, Power and Computing Technologies
abstract: DoS attack and intrusion prediction is essential for IoT networks because it guarantees service availability, and preserves reputation by reducing expensive downtime. Benign, infiltration traffic, DoS golden eye, hulk, slowloris, and slow http test classes were all not taken at the same time with high accuracy in earlier studies on DoS attack and intrusion detection. This research presents a stacking augmented explainable machine learning method for predicting multiclass DoS assaults and network intrusions. The relevant dataset was gathered from the Kaggle source and verified by cyber specialists. Chi-square, RFE, and mutual information are used in feature selection along with SMOTE-based data balance and preprocessing. SHAP is utilized for model explain ability, while grid search CV is used for hyper parameter tweaking. The best DoS attack and intrusion prediction model selection is examined using RF, XGBoost, catboost, LGBM, LR, and ensemble stacking technique (RF, XGB, LR). The stacking enriched ensemble strategy is chosen as the best prediction model in this paper with an accuracy of 97.953 percent. The accuracy of the suggested method is more than 1.75 percent higher than that of previous studies.

title: A Study of Cloud-Native Intrusion Detection Using VPC Flow Logs and Ensemble Learning
authors: Binny Thomas; Hisana Saji; Bhavya Shivani H; S Siva; R Sagara
abstract: Cloud computing has rapidly evolved into the foundational infrastructure for modern digital services, enabling organizations to deploy applications with unprecedented scalability, elasticity, and cost efficiency.However, the dynamic and distributed nature of cloud-native environments introduces complex security challenges that traditional intrusion detection systems are ill-equipped to address.Conventional IDS solutions depend on static network boundaries, deep packet inspection, and predefined attack signatures, all of which are increasingly ineffective in cloud environments dominated by encrypted traffic, ephemeral workloads, and software-defined networking.This study presents an extensive analysis of cloud-native intrusion detection systems that utilize Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) Flow Logs in conjunction with ensemble learning techniques.VPC Flow Logs provide scalable, lightweight, and privacy-preserving network traffic metadata, making them suitable for large-scale cloud monitoring.Ensemble learning methods combine multiple machine learning classifiers to enhance detection accuracy, reduce false positives, and improve robustness against evolving cyber threats.This paper systematically reviews existing research, explores architectural designs, analyzes detection methodologies, evaluates benefits and limitations, and discusses future research directions.The study demonstrates that ensemble-based intrusion detection using VPC Flow Logs offers a practical and effective solution for securing modern cloud infrastructures.

title: A Survey on Network Security: From Firewalls To Ai-Powered Threat Detection
authors: Navkiran Kaur Gill
venue: Journal of Advanced Research in Computer Technology & Software Applications
abstract: Over the years, network security has moved totally away from the original barbaric measures in defence and has moved on to even more sophisticated and complicated cyber threat opportunities to solve the problem. This paper presents a complete overview of network security measures, tracing the route of their evolution from outdated firewalls and intrusion detection systems (IDS) to such advanced AI technologies (AI)-based threat detection solutions. The research study introduces the reader to various security devices such as firewall, honeypots, and machine learning-based intrusion detection, among other security measures, as well as blockchain and quantum cryptography as well as new technologies. The main idea is using modern AI methods such as machine learning and behavioural analysis for the purpose of threats prevention. Besides, the paper may be identified as a communication link, sending data about honeypot attacks and IoT botnets and through the gained experience from various results. The research swathe presents the main concepts, challenges, and future paths in network security and takes a deep look into the requirement of continuous advancements to defend against the changes in the world of cyber threats. Through the analysis of multiple research contributions, the paper is a useful data one can use to understand the current situation and how network security is developing. DOI: https://doi.org/10.24321/3051.4304.202508

title: A Systematic Literature Review on Data-Efficient and Adaptive Learning Techniques for Encrypted Traffic Classification Under Modern Protocols
authors: Muntakimur Rahaman; Azwan Mahmud; Azlan Abd Aziz; Osama Abuajwa; Ji‐Jian Chin
abstract: Recent studies suggest that few-shot and zero-shot learning methods, drawing on meta-learning, self-supervised approaches and metric-learning ideas, can classify encrypted traffic (TLS 1.3 and QUIC) with competitive accuracy across different protocol conditions. This systematic literature review (SLR) investigates 22 studies selected from an initial pool of 500 papers using PRISMA 2020, focusing on current methodologies for non-stationary network traffic classification, with particular attention to few-shot, zero-shot, and meta-learning approaches. The research addresses four questions: (1) Which approaches have been employed for non-stationary network traffic classification and threat detection? (2) How do hybrid or cross-domain models improve adaptation, detection and overall efficiency? (3) What benchmarking standards exist for the datasets and evaluation metrics in use? (4) How do these methods address concept drift? This review identifies a range of approaches for capturing and analysing non-stationary network traffic but also reveals a significant gap in the empirical evidence addressing the last two questions. This points to a need for targeted experiments on continuously evolving network traffic and zero-day polymorphic attacks, both of which are central to the development of the next-generation adaptive intrusion-detection framework.

title: A Task-Label-Free Domain-Incremental Learning Framework for DDoS Detection in the Internet of Things
authors: Hong-Fei Wang; Heng-Yang Wang; Ge Zhu; Jin-Ping Tang
abstract: With the widespread application of Internet of Things (IoT) technologies, distributed denial of service (DDoS) attacks have become a core challenge threatening edge network security, yet traditional deep learning (DL) models commonly suffer from catastrophic forgetting in dynamic IoT traffic scenarios. To address this issue, we propose label-free ensemble progressive neural network (LFE-PNN), a framework specifically designed for low-resource edge environments. Through the design of lightweight expert columns (only 156.23-K parameters) and optimized lateral connection mechanisms, the framework effectively mitigates knowledge forgetting in domain incremental learning (DIL) while achieving a low inference latency of 2.88 ms. Unlike traditional progressive neural networks (PNNs) that rely on task labels for decision-making, we introduce a stacking-based metalearning mechanism to construct an adaptive decision fusion layer. This mechanism enables the model to automatically fuse multiexpert predictions without prior labels, thereby adapting to diverse IoT attack patterns in real-time. In the validation phase, we adopt four authoritative benchmark datasets, including Internet of Medical Things (IoMT), and specifically construct three real-world traffic datasets with high noise and structural diversity to simulate complex IoT operating environments. Experimental results show that LFE-PNN controls the average forgetting (AF) at $0.054{\,}\pm {\,}0.049$ and attains a detection accuracy of $99.53{\,}\pm {\,}0.11\%$ . Notably, in real-world IoT scenarios, the framework achieves an average accuracy gain of 35.21 percentage points, providing an efficient and practical technical path for security protection in dynamic IoT environments. Codes are available at https://github.com/Vincenzo1335/LFE-PNN

title: A two-stage deep learning approach for multiclass DGA-based malware communication detection and classification in DoH network traffic
authors: Hussein Abdumalik; Weiyan Hou; Yan Zhuang; Mirza Ali
abstract: The adoption of DNS over HTTPS (DoH) has substantially improved user privacy by encrypting DNS queries, but it has also introduced new opportunities for attackers to hide Domain Generation Algorithm (DGA)-based malware communications. In this study, we propose a novel two-stage deep learning framework that integrates an Autoencoder (AE) with Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks for detecting and classifying DGA-based malware in DoH traffic. The first stage employs an AE for dimensionality reduction and optimal feature extraction, followed by hybrid feature selection combining Random Forest (RF) importance scores and Mutual Information (MI). The second stage utilizes LSTM and GRU for binary and multiclass classification of malware families. To ensure robust evaluation, we employed stratified k-fold cross-validation (k = 5) and applied temporal SMOTE (tSMOTE) to training data to address class imbalance while avoiding data leakage. The proposed framework was evaluated on the CIRA-CIC-DoHBrw-2020 and DoH-DGA-Malware-Traffic-HKD datasets. AE-LSTM achieves 0.9958 accuracy for binary classification, while AE-GRU attains 0.9925 accuracy for multiclass classification. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework effectively identifies DGA-based malware in encrypted DoH traffic and outperforms standalone models across most evaluation metrics.

title: A Two-Stage Privacy-Aware SQL Anomaly Detector for Inline Database Defense
authors: Thanh-Tan Doan; Hung-Nghiep Tran
venue: International Conference on Multimedia Analysis and Pattern Recognition
abstract: Inline database defenses require mechanisms to intercept malicious attacks and performance anomalies. Conventional lexical filters lack awareness of query execution costs, while machine learning models trained on operational logs risk exposing sensitive proprietary data. This paper presents a privacy-aware SQL anomaly detector utilizing a two-phase architecture. The first phase employs deterministic screening to filter explicit SQL injection signatures and tautological constructs. For queries bypassing this phase, dynamic execution plan signals are first generated by the database optimizer. Subsequently, a deterministic pseudonymization protocol masks literal values and schema identifiers for secure telemetry and off-site analysis. The second phase utilizes an eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) classifier operating on an 11-dimensional bipartite feature space, combining the dynamic metrics with static structural features extracted from the pseudonymized text. Experimental evaluation on a hybrid dataset of 10,972 queries demonstrates that the proposed classifier achieves an F1 score of 0.9318 and a Matthews Correlation Coefficient of 0.8609. Performance profiling indicates an algorithmic inference latency of 1.471 μs and an integrated pipeline processing time of 2.692 ms. The integration of syntax analysis and execution plan metrics provides accurate anomaly detection within the strict latency constraints required for operational database firewalls. The source code and datasets are available at https://github.com/td-aiops-research-lab/PASAD

title: A101-23 Predictive Modeling of Respiratory Exacerbations Using Remote Patient Monitoring Data
authors: J Mehta; Nikitha Yerram; Saud Anwar; DENZIL M REID
venue: American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine
abstract: Abstract Rationale Early detection of respiratory exacerbations in patients with chronic respiratory diseases remains a critical unmet need. We hypothesized that integrating remote patient monitoring (RPM) data models with clinical and demographic factors could improve early risk stratification for exacerbations. Methods RPM data were collected from 50 patients (age range 13-86 yrs; mean 59.6 yrs; 54 % female) over three months, generating >1,000 daily measurements per patient. Variables included spirometry (FEV1, FVC, peak flow), oxygen saturation, demographic data, biologics use, and insurance type. Exacerbations were defined by clinically significant drops in FEV1, FVC, or SpO2, corroborated by alert counts. Logistic regression and k-nearest neighbors (k-NN) models were developed to predict high-risk events. Model performance was evaluated via accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV). Results The predictive model achieved 81 % overall accuracy, sensitivity 0.78, specificity 0.83, PPV 0.79, and NPV 0.82. Risk scores ranged from 0.16 to 0.91, and patients with ≥1 red alert had a 2.1-fold higher likelihood of adverse outcomes. Biologic use was associated with reduced exacerbation risk, while insurance type had no significant predictive impact. Conclusions AI-driven RPM models can effectively stratify respiratory patients by exacerbation risk, providing actionable insights for early clinical intervention. This approach has potential to reduce hospitalizations, optimize resource allocation, and personalize respiratory care. Future work will expand to larger cohorts and integrate additional biomarkers to enhance predictive accuracy. title: Achieving Interpretable DL-based Web Attack Detection through Malicious Payload Localization
authors: Pei-Yang Li; Fukun Mei; Ye Wang; Zhuotao Liu; Ke Xu; Chao Shen et al.
venue: Network and Distributed System Security Symposium
abstract: —Web attacks pose a significant threat to Web applications. While deep learning-based systems have emerged as promising solutions for detecting Web attacks, the lack of interpretability hinders their deployment in production. Existing interpretability methods are unable to explain Web attacks because they overlook the structure information of HTTP requests. They merely identify some important features, which are not understandable by security operators and fail to guide them toward effective responses. In this paper, we propose WebSpotter that achieves inter-pretable Web attack detection, which enhances existing deep learning-based detection methods by locating malicious payloads of the HTTP requests. It is inspired by the observation that malicious payloads often have a significant impact on the predictions of detection models. WebSpotter identifies the importance of each field of HTTP requests, and then utilizes a machine learning model to learn the correlation between the importance and malicious payloads. In addition, we demonstrate how WebSpotter can assist security operators in mitigating attacks by automatically generating WAF rules. Extensive evaluations on two public datasets and our newly constructed dataset demonstrate that WebSpotter significantly outperforms existing methods, achieving at least a 22% improvement in localization accuracy compared to baselines. We also conduct evaluations on real-world attacks collected from CVEs and real-world Web applications to illustrate the effectiveness of WebSpotter in practical scenarios.

title: ADAPTIVE CYBER INCIDENT RESPONSE METHOD FOR ENSURING DEPENDABILITY OF INFORMATION SYSTEMS IN SITUATION CENTERS
authors: В. Ф. Гречанінов
abstract: The paper develops an adaptive cyber incident response method aimed at ensuring the dependability of informationsystems used in situation centers under conditions of increasing cyber threats, growing complexity of information systemarchitectures, and higher requirements for the continuity of critical services. The relevance of the study is determined bythe need for timely detection of cyber incidents, assessment of their impact on the state of information systems, andautomated generation of decisions to maintain the required level of dependability. The purpose of the research is todevelop an adaptive cyber incident response method based on intelligent security event analysis, risk assessment, anddynamic selection of countermeasures. A review of current approaches to ensuring the dependability of informationsystems in situation centers, cyber incident response methods, and decision support technologies is conducted. Amathematical model for assessing the impact of cyber incidents on dependability indicators is proposed, and the adaptiveresponse process is formalized. The developed method includes security event monitoring, incident classification,criticality assessment, threat evolution forecasting, and selection of an optimal response strategy. In addition, anarchitecture of an intelligent decision support system for ensuring the dependability of information systems in situationcenters is proposed. Simulation results confirmed the effectiveness of the approach in increasing the level of dependability,reducing cyber incident response time, decreasing the risk of disruption of information resources, and improving systemresilience to destructive impacts. The obtained results can be applied in the design, modernization, and operation ofinformation systems in situation centers, as well as in the development of intelligent cybersecurity management tools andmechanisms for ensuring operational continuity.Keywords: situation center, dependability, cyber incident, adaptive response, information system, intelligentsystem, decision support, mathematical model, risk management, cybersecurity. title: Adaptive Feature Clustering Algorithm and Real-Time Intrusion Detection Model for Encrypted Malicious Traffic
authors: Qihang Li
abstract: With the widespread adoption of encryption technology in network communication, encrypted traffic, while protecting user privacy and data security, is also being abused by attackers. Traditional intrusion detection methods based on plaintext analysis have become ineffective. Accurate identification and real-time detection of encrypted malicious traffic has become a core challenge in the field of network security. Existing encrypted malicious traffic detection methods suffer from shortcomings such as non-adaptive feature extraction, low clustering accuracy, high detection latency, and difficulty in dealing with new and unknown encrypted malicious traffic, failing to meet the real-time protection needs in complex network environments. To address this, this paper first designs an adaptive feature clustering algorithm (AFC algorithm) to automatically mine deep hidden features of encrypted traffic to achieve dynamic clustering and updating of malicious traffic features. Secondly, based on the clustering results, a lightweight real-time intrusion detection model integrating a feature attention mechanism and a lightweight classifier is constructed to balance detection accuracy and real-time performance. Finally, its effectiveness is verified through multi-scenario experiments. Experiments based on public datasets such as CIC-Darknet 2020 and ISCX VPN, as well as real network traffic data, show that the AFC algorithm achieves the highest clustering accuracy on all three datasets, reaching 94%, 93%, and 95% respectively, representing an average improvement of 11% compared to the K-means algorithm and 8% compared to the DBSCAN algorithm. In terms of misclassification rate, the AFC algorithm performs best, with misclassification rates of only 4%, 5%, and 3% across the three datasets. This is significantly lower than the two traditional algorithms and outperforms existing mainstream detection methods, effectively identifying both known and unknown encrypted malicious traffic, thus meeting the needs of real-time intrusion detection.

title: Adaptive Hybrid Adversarial Training for Robust Deep Learning-Based Network Intrusion Detection
authors: Samuel Okechukwu Nnaji
abstract: Abstract: Deep Learning (DL) has become central to modern Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDS), yet convolutional and recurrent detectors remain highly susceptible to adversarial perturbations that can silently flip malicious traffic into benign predictions. Existing single-technique adversarial training approaches, most commonly built around the Fast Gradient Sign Method (FGSM) or Projected Gradient Descent (PGD) alone, improve robustness against the specific perturbation family used in training but generalize poorly to unseen attack strategies and often erode clean-data accuracy. This study proposes an Adaptive Hybrid Adversarial Training (AHAT) framework that combines multiple adversarial example generators (FGSM, PGD, and Carlini–Wagner) under an epoch-adaptive curriculum scheduler, fused with a hybrid Convolutional Neural Network–Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (CNN-BiLSTM) detector and a composite loss that jointly penalizes clean-sample error, adversarial-sample error, and a consistency term between clean and adversarial representations. The framework was evaluated using a quantitative experimental design on benchmark-style network flow data structured after the NSL-KDD and CICIDS2017 traffic schemas, with illustrative/simulated results used to demonstrate the evaluation pipeline pending full empirical deployment. Under this illustrative pipeline, the proposed AHAT model sustained a mean adversarial detection accuracy of 89.1% across FGSM, PGD, and Carlini–Wagner attacks, compared with 82.6% for ensemble adversarial training, 76.9% for standard single-method adversarial training, and 27.5% for an undefended baseline CNN, while clean accuracy was retained at 98.3%. These findings suggest that adaptive, curriculum-driven hybridization of attack families and model architectures offers a more balanced robustness–accuracy trade-off than static, single-technique adversarial training. The paper contributes a reproducible architecture, a composite loss formulation, and an evaluation protocol that other researchers can instantiate on live SPSS-analyzed or network-captured datasets. Implications for security operations centres, cyber-defense policy in developing-country contexts, and future research on certifiably robust NIDS are discussed. Keywords: Adversarial Training; Network Intrusion Detection; Deep Learning; Robustness; Curriculum Learning; CNN-BiLSTM; Cybersecurity. title: Adaptive Sequence-Embedded Gradient Boosting for Real-Time Phishing Website Detection
authors: T. Elangovan; P. S.; Chandru S; Kaleeswaran S
venue: International Conference on Information Security and Cryptology
abstract: Phishing threats keep changing, exploiting the properties of static URLs and the dynamic aspects of the website to defraud victims, making the traditional methods of detection inadequate. In this paper, a new hybrid phishingdetection model that combines sequence-aware embeddings with Gradient Boosting is proposed, which outperforms in terms of predictive accuracy and flexibility. Embedded scripts and URLs are coded as sequential patterns by a lightweight embedding layer, and structural and temporal patterns are recovered, which are not usually used by feature-based methods. The embeddings are then fused with traditional features, such as domain attributes, SS/TLS certificate metadata, and HTML indicators, resulting in a complete representation of the behaviour of websites. An adaptive Gradient Boosting classifier is applied to the integrated feature set and ranks features according to their dynamically changing usefulness to overcome already developed phishing techniques. Experimental analysis on various real-life datasets, the classification accuracy is above 99%, outperforming conventional methods such as XGBoost, Random Forest, and SVM methods, while also maintaining low false-positive rates. The feature importance analysis offers interpretability for cybersecurity professionals, enabling them to take appropriate actions accordingly. The proposed system can be deployed at scale in browser extensions, enterprise security systems, and automated threat intelligence platforms, providing proactive protection against increasingly sophisticated phishing attacks.

title: AdSeeker: An Agent-Driven Framework for Automated Malicious Ad Detection in Mobile Apps
authors: Yi Zhang; Shanshan Wang; Zhen-Xiang Chen; Bo Yang; Shan Zhen; Zhen Wang
venue: Annual IEEE Communications Society Conference on Sensor, Mesh and Ad Hoc Communications and Networks
abstract: Online advertisements (ads) play a critical role in sustaining the mobile ecosystem. However, imperfect ad review mechanisms allow ads to be exploited as a channel for malicious content dissemination, posing significant security risks to users and platforms. Existing malicious advertisement detection methods heavily rely on manually crafted rules, which limit automation and undermine detection robustness in complex and dynamic environments. To address these limitations, this paper proposes AdSeeker, an automated malicious ad detection framework driven by an autonomous agent. AdSeeker leverages the agent’s decision-making capability to systematically explore application interfaces and collect multi-dimensional ad-related evidence, including ad SDK metadata, permission usage, network redirection links, and ad image elements. Based on the collected evidence, AdSeeker classifies malicious ad behaviors, assesses risk levels, and provides remediation suggestions, enabling quantitative security evaluation of mobile applications. We evaluate AdSeeker on 30,000 applications from AndroZoo. The results show that 10,497 apps contain ads, from which 14,971 ad samples are collected, including 1,537 malicious ads. AdSeeker achieves a detection precision of 96.30%. Our findings further reveal that malicious ads are present even in legitimate applications, highlighting the necessity for strengthened ad network auditing and more effective malicious ad governance to foster a safer mobile ecosystem. The source code is publicly available on GitHub at https://github.com/AnaY1115/AdSeeker.
